The result has allowed England to top Group 3 of League A in the Nations League.

#1893. Scotland year that started with promise ends in another setback amid fears over one player’s career

A year that started so full of promise for Scotland ground to a humiliating halt in St Gallen. The 13th match of a World Cup dominated 12 months always threatened to be the toughest of tough tasks.

Not perhaps as challenging as taking on Brazil in Miami or Morocco in Boston. But Switzerland, World Cup quarter-finalists themselves, are no pushovers, as they proved in a match of supposedly little consequence for them. Having already secured top place in Group B1, they enjoyed the luxury of making changes and still eased to a deserved 4-0 victory in the university city.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

What did Sebastien Pocognoli learn? Not too much as he watched his side picked apart by Murat Yakin’s exciting team. Two goals just after the break – a tap in from Winsley Boteli and a rocket from Alvyn Sanches – rendered the second half little more than a training exercise.

Substitute Zeki Amdouni wrapped things up in the final minute with a shot from the edge of the of the box that took a wicked deflection off Luke Graham. It was that kind of night. Lewis Ferguson had put through his own goal to set the Swiss on their way after 22 minutes.

It was anything but the much-needed statement result for Pocognoli some had surmised might be possible against hosts who could afford to coast. Instead, there were fears that Switzerland – 3-0 up after just 51 minutes – would pile on the pain.

Scotland suffered a 7-0 defeat against Uruguay 80 or so miles away in Basel at the 1954 World Cup and something as embarrassing felt possible, particularly when the "oles" from the home fans were ringing around the Sitterstadion early in the second half.

This wasn’t how Andy Robertson, who had 103 stitched into the tongues of his boots, wanted to become Scotland’s most-capped ever men’s player. Scotland were completely licked.

Sanches missed an open goal with eight minutes left after Angus Gunn miscued a pass, although the Swiss forward was around 50 yards out. The keeper did well to block a later shot from the same player but was helpless when Amdouni’s deflected effort looped into the net for 4-0.

Of course, it helps when the opposition scores the all-important first goal for you. Ferguson inadvertently put through his own net as he attempted to cut out the danger following Zachary Athekame’s cross from the right. Not too long afterwards, about 900 miles away in Skopje, Slovenia scored their opener against North Macedonia to further put the Scots behind the black ball in their quest to finish in second place. The Slovenians ended up winning 3-0, leaving Scotland in a very distant third place in the group and wondering what the future holds. At least there are no more games until March. It’s been a tough old year. The memorable moments have almost all occurred off the pitch. It isn’t all on Pocognoli, granted.

What was underlined here is that the Belgian could do with a bit of fortune. He could do with the stars aligning in the way they did for Steve Clarke a year ago this week, when everything seemed to fall into place eventually on a night of nights against Denmark in Glasgow.

Pocognoli, by contrast, is struggling to get going. His Hampden bow against Switzerland was ruined by Jack Hendry’s red card just ten minutes in. Here he saw Scott McTominay blaze over from six yards and watched John McGinn place a header straight into the hands of keeper Yvon Mvogo.

More serious woe arrived in the form of the latest injury misery to befall Aaron Hickey. The former Hearts player’s left hamstring has proved troublesome for a few managers, including Clarke, and obviously for the player himself.

It was heartbreaking to see the player stumble having performed a typically diligent defensive duty, in this case mopping up by directing a header into Gunn’s arms. He also pulled something in the process and made a sad exit down the tunnel after 36 minutes, with Nathan Patterson replacing him. Brentford will be furious although it’s not as if Pocognoli hadn’t sought to manage the player’s minutes.

He left him out of the first game of the window against North Macedonia. This latest setback feels bigger than just what it means for Pocognoli and Scotland. It raises real fears about a brilliant young player’s career.

So the outcome of the match, as dispiriting as the defeat was, needs to be placed in context. It might have proved a happier evening had Hickey’s header from Andy Robertson’s cross 24 minutes sneaked in rather than past the post just minutes after Ferguson’s own goal horror.

Hickey was also in the thick of things after a clever touch from Oli McBurnie saw him burst into the Swiss half. Kieran Tierney was to his left and was screaming to be played in but the wing-back just could not get the ball out of his feet and the chance was gone.

Ferguson’s misery was all the more frustrating because it was so unnecessary. Ryan Porteous was waiting to clear but the Bologna midfielder got in before him and steered past Gunn while attempting to clear the danger.

The game was over six minutes into the second half. Ballet exchanged passes with Remo Feuler and shot towards goal. Although Boteli probably didn’t need to help the ball over the line, he did anyway at the risk of seeing the goal chalked off for offside.

He was just onside and was credited with the strike. There was no doubt who scored the third for the hosts, with Sanches latching on to a loose ball after Patterson had been dispossessed before rifling into the corner past Gunn.

The loss of a fourth goal seemed inconsequential but did seem to sum everything up. These are very different times to 12 months ago and more hurt may lie ahead.

#1892. Sebastien Pocognoli optimistic about Scotland future after heavy defeat as he identifies ‘next step’

Sebastien Pocognoli has insisted Scotland’s bruising 4-0 defeat to Switzerland was not a fair reflection of the contest as their Nations League campaign ended on a sour note in St Gallen.

A second-half collapse against a second-string Swiss side who had already secured promotion to League A condemned the Scots to their heaviest loss since their 5-1 thrashing by Germany at Euro 2024.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The result leaves Pocognoli's men third in Group B1 with seven points from six matches. It also means Scotland will enter the Euro 2028 qualifying draw in Belfast in a couple of weeks in pot three, potentially presenting a more challenging route towards the tournament.

However, the head coach was keen to highlight the positives from his side's performance, particularly their first-half display, arguing that the final scoreline was harsh on his players.

“The score is heavy with the 4-0, but I don't think it's a reflection of the game, if I'm really honest and objective," Pocognoli said. “We had some very good moments in the game, we started the game like we wanted, aggressive away from home. We could decide to be low on the pitch, but we did what we wanted to plan.”

Lewis Ferguson's unfortunate own goal handed Switzerland the advantage, but the visitors responded well and created opportunities through Andy Robertson, Aaron Hickey and John McGinn.

Pocognoli felt his side had done enough to trouble the hosts before the interval, despite failing to convert their promising openings.

"We played a good first half, we created chances, we were dominant in some moments in the game, and we faced Switzerland with different shapes and adapted well from the first minute,” he continued. “We conceded the goal from maybe one of the first chances they had. We also created chances, but we missed it. It means we were not clinical in that moment in the box.”

The second half, however, exposed Scotland's defensive vulnerabilities in alarming fashion. The Swiss scored twice within six minutes of the restart through Winsley Boteli and Alvyn Sanches, effectively ending the contest.

Pocognoli admitted his team’s start to the second period was unacceptable, adding: “We started poorly from the first minute, a poor corner we gave away. Then you feel that, OK, we will get punished. But I think when we made the substitutions, they made an impact, and we should have scored two goals in that period.

“We got punished for the same reason like in the first half. At the end, it's a bad feeling, the score, but I think that the players try to do their best and create moments that we want to see.”

Despite the emphatic nature of the defeat, the Belgian was adamant there were enough encouraging signs that his players were beginning to understand his more progressive style, even if the execution remains inconsistent.

“If we were in confidence, we would not produce the moments we produce in the game," he summarised. “We create good moments on the ball, on pure bravery decisions to play forward through the lines or the pressure. We create chances also for pressing, sometimes we should have to manage better the transition from pressing, but it is all the things we want to see.

“So the next step is to have the quality to just finish this action, and the more we have games together, the more we will try to fix these things. We have a lot of good response from this camp and it's good for the future as well.”

#1886. Jurgen Klopp calls for Gianni Infantino to be replaced as FIFA president – ‘Worse than Sepp Blatter’

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 09:47, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 09:48

Germany head coach Jurgen Klopp has called for a change in FIFA leadership as he believes that president Gianni Infantino is worse than disgraced predecessor Sepp Blatter.

Infantino has spent the last 10 years in the most powerful position in global football and has frequently faced criticism, but widespread backlash aimed at the 56-year-old Swiss chief has grown since the 2026 World Cup.

In the summer, Infantino came under fire for his involvement in overturning a red card suspension for USA striker Folarin Balogun following a phone call from U.S. President Donald Trump.

Infantino's position at FIFA was plunged into a deeper crisis when he announced controversial plans to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

This attracted major opposition from several football confederations including UEFA, who threatened to boycott FIFA tournaments, but the ‘FIFA Forward Enterprises’ has since been scrapped.

Infantino became FIFA president in 2016 after former chief Blatter stepped down amid a ​major corruption scandal that lead to him facing criminal charges.

Infantino was then re-elected unopposed in 2019 and 2023, and intends to stand again for a fourth term in March, but Klopp is one high-profile figure keen for change at the very top of football.

Indeed, the Germany boss made his feelings clear on Infantino during a press conference ahead of Germany’s UEFA Nations League showdown with the Netherlands on Monday.

“The general consensus is that a change might make sense,” the former Liverpool manager told reporters.

“After Sepp Blatter, we thought things couldn’t get any worse, and then we managed to pull it off.

“There are certainly people who care about football and have no financial interests. If one of them were to take over, it would be absolutely helpful.”

While working as a pundit before taking the Germany job earlier this year, Klopp slammed the decision for Balogun’s red card to be overturned at the World Cup, and was particularly critical of Trump’s apparent involvement.

“If that really was the case, then that’s crazy,” Klopp said in July. “Let’s just say: this is our game, not theirs.

“These two people (Trump and Infantino), who both have no idea about football, should have nothing to do with that. That was a red card. There’s no two ways about it.”

Klopp was appointed Germany head coach a few weeks later, replacing Julian Nagelsmann following the country’s shock last-32 exit on penalties to Paraguay at the World Cup.

The 59-year-old has not publicly stated who he would like to see take the FIFA presidency from Infantino, but former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega and Japan Football Association president Kozo Tashima have announced their intention to challenge him.

Meanwhile, former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger has decided not to stand against Infantino as a candidate in FIFA’s presidential election, despite allegedly receiving backing from France president Emmanuel Macron.

Wenger - who had distanced himself from Infantino’s aborted FIFA Forward Enterprises plan - currently holds the role of Head of Global Development at FIFA and is expected to continue in this position.

Moving abroad makes you grow up, and if you pick the right club, your game improves tenfold. Looking back at Jadon going to Man United at that point, I would have stayed in Dortmund.

“As long as Jadon gets his creative head back on, because he's definitely a threat when he has the ball. He's got to get that back. You could see it happening, and he wouldn't be adverse to it as long as he has the fire and hunger, because he has the ability. He just has to pick the right club to give him that platform to express himself again, that could be Celtic.”

#1884. Ex-Celtic and Hibs boss forced to quit managerial role for a second time due to ‘health issues’

Former Celtic and Hibs head coach Tony Mowbray has been forced to step down from his role at EFL Championship outfit Blackburn Rovers due to health issues.

Mowbray, 62, returned to the dugout at Ewood Park for a second time in the summer, having previously managed the club between 2017 and 2022, where he led Blackburn to 13th in the table after winning six of his first 15 games in charge of the club.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

However, in an emotional statement on the club’s official website, Mowbray has now confirmed he has departed his role as manager, with assistant Mike Dodds placed in temporary charge.

Previously head coach at Birmingham City, he stepped away from his role at St Andrew’s in early 2024 due to health reasons, later revealing he had been undergoing treatment for bowel cancer, though he was eventually given the all-clear following treatment.

A statement on Blackburn’s website read: “Unfortunately, due to health issues, I have to step back from my role as head coach of Blackburn Rovers. I'm immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I've loved working with them.

“Thank you to my coaching staff for all your hard work and for the support you've given me. It's been a pleasure working alongside you. To the fans, thank you for the way you've supported me and the team this season. I've always tried to give you a team that you can be proud of. Your support has meant a great deal to me."

In response, Blackburn chief executive officer Steve Curwood said: “Tony's passion for the club and his professionalism are clear to see, but it is his kindness and the care he shows for players, staff and those around him that mean so much. Our priority now is to make sure he feels that same care and support from all of us. We will support him and his family in every way we can.”

During his successful management career, Mowbray led West Bromwich Albion and Blackburn to promotion and, more recently, took Sunderland to the EFL Championship playoffs in 2023. At Hibs, he won the Scottish Football Writers' Association manager of the year award, spending two years at Easter Road between 2004 and 2006.

He returned to the Scottish Premiership with Celtic, whom he represented over 75 times during his playing career in the summer of 2009. However, a lack of domestic success saw him relieved of his duties the following March.

#1883. Ramos speaks out after disappointing Portugal result vs. Denmark: “Something that happens”

AC Milan are, once again, left looking at a disappointing performance from Goncalo Ramos; this time it was for Portugal.

It’s fair to say that Ramos’ start to life with Milan has been unsatisfactory. The Portuguese started brightly in his first two games, but has since struggled to really hit the highs expected of him after an almost €90 million deal was agreed in the summer.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

With another international break, the hope was that he’d rediscover the form from the last set of games and bring it back to San Siro, but it hasn’t happened that way yet.

Speaking in the mixed zone after Portugal’s heavy defeat, Ramos looked at what went wrong in the game and what needs to be corrected next time, as MilanPress relays.

“I think it was a tough match. They studied our team well, and even the details ultimately fell in their favour. Then we ended up losing momentum a bit, but that’s something that happens and is part of it.

“We’re first in the most important group. We already have another match in three days, so it’s not worth dwelling too much on what happened today. There’s already a match ahead, and it’s very important.”

“In the end, they managed to apply better pressure on us. We weren’t able to find many options, and that ended up hurting our game because we like to have clean, controlled possession of the ball, and that’s what makes the difference in our game.

“On the one hand, it’s good to have a match in three days and not have to spend three or four months thinking about a defeat like that. We already have a game to respond and to erase what happened here today.

“The conversation in the locker room after the game was that we’re first and we have a game to clean up after what happened today. That’s the goal of the team and the group.”

Considering he’s now the out-and-out first-choice striker for Portugal, it’s a lot of pressure on his shoulders for club and country. Hopefully he can start to thrive under the pressure, rather than succumbing to it.

#1882. England versus Spain becoming a new 'clásico' as Leeds United keeper James Trafford announces himself on world stage

That's how widely-respected Spanish sports newspaper Marca described La Roja's rivalry with England following the Three Lions' stunning Sunday-best victory at the Metropolitano. High praise indeed.

That it is becoming one of the most absorbing and significant in world football is surely beyond doubt now.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

In terms of beating the world champions, England have been here before. Back in November 2011, a screamer from Frank Lampard secured a Wembley victory against the feted Spanish, who were also European Championship holders at the same time.

This felt different. On that aforesaid occasion, England prevailed following a backs-to-the-wall performance which saw them pinned back in their own half for long spells against dominant opponents. They converted one of just two chances that came their way.

By contrast, Sunday saw those in white subjugate Spain with an elite showing.

Certainly for 65 to 70 minutes, the hosts' much-vaunted midfield—Arsenal duo Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino, alongside Fabián Ruiz and Alex Baena—were suffocated by England's high press.

It was an intense game plan executed 'with the precision of a master tailor' in the words of Marca. Ruiz and Merino both got the hook at half-time.

The narrative only changed when Elliot Anderson received his marching orders.

The hosts roared back and things became undeniably hairy in the final quarter. But unlike against Argentina in Atlanta in July, Thomas Tuchel's substitutions did not see England adopt a defensive straitjacket.

Leeds United's Dominic Calvert-Lewin came on as the visitors focused on staying higher up the pitch, if at all possible, amid serious late pressure from Spain.

It ended in a merited 3-2 win for the English. In three of the last four meetings between these two, a team has triumphed by the odd goal in five.

England triumphed by the same scoreline and in similar fashion to their previous visit to Spain back in October 2018 - in another Nations League encounter played out in Seville, this time. Again, they achieved success by being proactive as opposed to parking the bus.

Fabulous counter-attacking strikes from Raheem Sterling (2) and Marcus Rashford put the visitors 3-0 up to silence the Spanish hordes. It was the prelude to a strong home fightback in the second half, but no victory.

On this occasion, England's physical and tactical dominance was even more sustained and their third goal, scored by Ben White on 57 minutes, finished off a move of the highest order.

For too long in the past, certainly before that 2018 occasion in Seville, England had been cowed on their visits to Spain. In their previous four matches, all defeats, they failed to score. Ever since Gary Lineker, then at Barcelona, struck all four goals in a stunner at Madrid's Bernebeu Stadium in February 1987.

England have now regained the full respect of international football's undoubted success story of the current century. The team who, alongside France, are the current benchmark for all other nations.

Sunday night was undeniably sweetened by the fact that Spain relinquished their magnificent 44-game unbeaten sequence in the process.

That run included a 2-1 win over England in the Euro 2024 final in Berlin and this summer’s World Cup.

Spain's previous defeat was back in March 2023 against Scotland in Glasgow.

On an evening when the usual suspects came to the party in the shape of Jude Bellingham, whose pass for White's goal was delectable and Harry Kane, others also accepted their invites.

What a night for Leeds's James Trafford for instance. His fantastic double save late on to deny Fer Lopez and Aymeric Laporte announced his arrival on the world stage.

It presents Tuchel with a genuine headache - a welcome one, that said - regarding who will be his bonafide No 1 in 2027.

The battle between Trafford and Jordan Pickford is now a proper fight. It's not quite Peter Shilton versus Ray Clemence levels in the 1970s and early 80s just yet, but it might be heading in that direction. Tellingly, Trafford started both Nations League games against Spain, as opposed to his Everton rival.

Remember, remember the month of November? England will.

Sunday's success was a statement win of the ilk of 2015 when they beat the French 2-0 at Wembley and a decade earlier, in the same month, when a late brace from Michael Owen saw them triumph 3-2 against bitter foes Argentina, in Geneva of all places. Let's hope on this occasion, they build on it.

#1881. SFA must row back on all-in Sebastien Pocognoli gamble as Scotland fear ultimate custard pie

Taxi for Sebastien Pocognoli? Or should that be cable car? Scotland suffered in Switzerland on Monday and appear to be on a very slippery slope.

Steve Clarke endured two 4-0 defeats in his first five matches in charge so let no one argue that heavy beatings alone are sackable offences. But Pocognoli is sorely aware that he is treading on thin ice in the court of public opinion following a 4-0 drubbing against Switzerland in St Gallen, a gateway to the Alps.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He won’t need to look at the main Tartan Army fans’ forum, where the most visited thread is titled simply: sack him.

The numbers commenting suggests a healthy debate is occurring. Although a few are backing him, or at least who are pointing out that six games is not long enough to judge anyone, they are in the minority.

Of course, a lot of this is the usual ‘look at me and my extreme opinion’ showboating. Heaven knows, there was enough of that on X in the aftermath of Scotland’s latest reversal. Everyone’s an expert. Everyone knew better although, in the case of Pocognoli, maybe they did.

He was told Ben Gannon-Doak isn’t a wing-back and he was told that what is good for a game against North Macedonia might not necessarily be what is required against a team like Switzerland. The double midfield pivot of Lewis Ferguson and Billy Gilmour? Isn’t working. Again, a conclusion many reached at the end of the last window, long before the wretched night in a charming Swiss hamlet. Once known as the capital of embroidery, St Gallen is where things began unstitching very badly indeed for Scotland’s new manager after a heavy and cheerless defeat.

It was as concerning as it was sore. After all, Switzerland played what their fans explained was a B team and yet still had the game won inside 51 minutes. The "oles" had started. If the Swiss weren’t such a polite lot, we might have been treated to a rendition of: "Are you Liechtenstein in disguise?"

It’s just as well the Nations League format has changed otherwise Scotland could be looking at a relegation play-off against the Faroe Islands – unbeaten in six Nations League games – to avoid demotion to League C.

Scotland are not world beaters but they are better than this. They are better than finishing a distant third in a group where they are ranked seven places higher than the team that did in fact finish in second place: Slovenia. That’s underachievement writ large, whether someone is finding his feet or not. There’s giving a manager time and then there’s expecting the bare minimum.

No wonder there’s anger. No wonder there’s bemusement at the SFA appearing so beholden to the gospel according to Pocognoli that they have permitted his ideas about tactics to cascade throughout the entire set-up. As Under-21 coach Tony Docherty stated a few weeks ago, his side will be a “mirror image” of the A side. Gadzooks. And further down the chain, including the likes of the Under-15s and Under-16s? All working in the same, uniform way, Docherty confirmed.

Memo to the SFA: stop wasting time arranging friendlies in Boston and start rowing back on this one-size-fits-all formula. It could negatively impact Scottish football for generations. In many people's eyes, Pocognoli is already done after a reign lasting barely 90 days.

Getting him out means forking out the compensation fee but it also means telling the phalanx of new coaches – as many as ten have been appointed at various age levels – to ditch the high line, the three defenders and ‘box’ midfield. It means turning Hampden upside down.

It is, nevertheless, a good time to sack someone. If the international window is prime time for clubs to ditch unwanted managers then surely it’s optimal for an international team to do so now: in this long gap between international matches.

Scotland’s next competitive international could be as long away as next September if they are drawn in a four-team group for the Euros. Pocognoli, who turned 39 just before he took the job, could be in his 40s before Scotland next play a match of consequence.

Of course, there is one very important looming date: Sunday 6 December. Pocognoli – or at least we must assume at the time of writing that it will be Pocognoli – will be present and correct in the International Convention Centre in Belfast for the draw for Euro 2028 qualifying.

Ian Maxwell, the SFA chief executive, will be beside him to face some no doubt awkward questions. One of them will be, where are Scotland going? Because from this angle, it looks like backwards. They are at risk of being splatted with international football’s biggest custard pie: failing to qualify for a tournament they are co-hosting. Now assured pot three in the draw, it’s possible they miss out.

The post-World Cup malaise might well have been unavoidable. Even with Clarke in charge there would have been a likely drop-off. The natives were already restless. Away from the traffic cone malarkey, away from the baseball and boozing, it’s been a dreadful year for the national team.

Six defeats out of 13 matches and just five wins, the only one of any real worth being the 1-0 victory over Haiti and even that drew criticism for not being comprehensive enough. Three defeats in six Nations League games, two of which came at Hampden, suggests it’s going from bad to worse under Pocognoli.

The SFA have been criticised for milking the summer trip to Massachusetts to the max, with reports of a biennial friendly match being arranged at Fenway Park or elsewhere. A hat tip to Boston’s boys of summer might be acceptable if Maxwell and co invoke the fundamental rule of baseball in relation to Pocognoli: Three strikes and you’re out. They won’t and neither should they.

Three defeats in six matches is not a sacking offence. But an appointment the SFA seemed very pleased with themselves to acknowledge was data-led now looks increasingly at risk of an outage.

By Darren Plant | 16 Nov 2026 10:16, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 10:17

Everton and Nottingham Forest are reportedly ready to do battle for Gremio defender Gustavo Martins.

Twenty-one of his 24 appearances for Gremio this season have come from the starting lineup. Gremio currently sit in 18th position in the Brasileiro table.

If Gremio are relegated to the second tier, they are likely to be inundated with offers for a player in Martins whose contract is due to expire in December 2027.

Regardless, Gremio have allegedly already set an asking price in the region of €12m (£10.02m) to €15m (£12.52m).

With a strong Brazilian contingent at Forest, there are clear reasons as to why Martins may be interested in signing for Forest.

However, they already have four senior centre-back options who have long-term contracts in place at the City Ground.

In sharp contrast, two of Everton's top three central defenders - James Tarkowski and Michael Keane - are 33 years of age, while Moyes is generally short of strength-in-depth.

Bayern Munich are thinking about life after Manuel Neuer and are looking for a long-term successor to their historic goalkeeper.

The advantage of this recruitment strategy is that it allows Risser to continue to progress at the northern club until the end of this season.

However, Bayern Munich are not alone in the race, as five other European heavyweights are interested: Manchester City, Liverpool, Manchester United, Inter Milan and Juventus. Lens are reportedly demanding at least £34m (€40m).

#1870. Bradford City boss Michael Duff on working relationship with Alex Morris - and praise for stalwart duo

Alexander's partnership with assistant Chris Lucketti was a winning one, with coaches Mark Trueman and Colin Doyle also being key components to the Bantams' upturn.

Early days it may be for Duff, but the Bantams chief is quick to value the input of his own number two in Alex Morris and the aforesaid coaching duo who have been stalwarts at the club in recent years.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Duff, whose side are preparing for back-to-back home league derbies with Doncaster Rovers and Barnsley, said: "Truey's been in the club for a long time and worked under a few managers.

"Quite often it can be: 'Oh, here we go, here's another one, what's he going to do, what's he going to say?'

"But I've had some good conversations with Truey and him and Doyler have been really, really good. But they couldn't beat me and Alex at padel, I'll throw that one in!

"Sometimes, it's little things in training. We review every training session and sometimes it's a case of 'Well, they wouldn't have been used to that because of this' or 'They might not like that because of this'.

"It's like: 'Okay, well that's good to know.' That's where we (Duff and Morris) may need to check ourselves and go: 'Okay, what's the best thing for the team ultimately'."

Duff and Morris enjoyed a strong working relationship during their time together at previous club Wycombe Wanderers, with Duff moving quickly to sound out Morris about heading north and renewing their union when the opportunity presented itself at Valley Parade.

He acknowledges that his deputy is particularly important for daily dialogue with players, as his assistant position allows him to develop a more up-close-and-personal relationship.

The City boss continued: "Alex spends a lot more time with the players than I do because he's around them a lot more often and they'll probably have more personal conversations with Alex. It's something he's very good at.

"I try to, but obviously sometimes when you speak to a player, it's like: 'Well, he's the headmaster, so tell him what he wants and get out,' which I don't want it to be like that. But that's just the natural evolution of my job.

"Alex is good for many different reasons. Tactically, he's very, very good and has been coaching for a long, long time.

"He's coached at a high level. He's worked with League Two players and worked at Championship level, so he can put on different sessions and knows what the group needs and knows me as well.

"Sometimes that's where assistants are really good, because it's like: 'I know you want to do this, but this might not be right at the moment'. And that's where sometimes I have to check my own ego, because it's not about me.

"He's a really good sort of sounding board because he knows me really well."

#1869. Worthing Women: Make Mackay-ne a double!

Nicole Mackay’s brace made it three goals in two games for her and a second successive win for Worthing Women, as they saw off Aylesford at the Sussex Transport Community Stadium.

After last week’s epic cup comeback at Camden, teenage starlet Hattie Rainey made her full debut while Ruby Murdock also came into the starting eleven; meaning that Skye Birkinshaw and Cristie Pritchard began on the bench.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Barely had supporters sat in their seats than the aforementioned Mackay got the home team off and running, just three minutes in.

Seizing on  a loose ball on the edge of the eighteen yard area, the in-form striker drilled low and hard into Aylesford ‘keeper Sade Rider’s bottom right-hand corner, to open the scoring in emphatic fashion.

Although a very different picture might have been painted had the Rebels's netminder Sian Woods not denied a clean through Leigha Bradding-Butler not once but twice, to deny the visitor’s top scorer a seventh strike of a prolific campaign.

Still inside the opening ten minutes, Mackay came the width of the crossbar away from extending the host’s advantage. Dusting herself down and stepping up to take a free-kick she herself had won, the ball cannoned back off the frame of the goal, with Jess Richardson landing the rebound on top of the net.

The game settled into a more even contest for some time after that, as Worthing pressed forward in search of a second before the break, with Aylesford looking dangerous on the counter-attack.

Approaching the half-time interval, an audible sigh of relief reverberated around Woodside Road via Immy Armstrong - a threat from her set-pieces - firing narrowly over the target from inside the penalty area.

The sun then broke through the clouds on a pleasant November afternoon; similar to the way in which Aliyah Sheridan did when gifted possession by the homester’s otherwise solid last line of defence. Woods redeemed herself via a strong parry to her left of Sheridan’s subsequent shot.

One final opportunity before the change of ends fell to visiting Skipper Ami Burnham, only for Woods to keep her out by way of another excellent stop.

It’s tight at the bottom of the London & South East Prem but it was the Reds who headed into the interval with a precious one-goal lead.

Worthing continued to probe and were rewarded just shy of the hour mark, thanks to the persistence of Mackay. Although it was centre-half Ella Terry who got the ball rolling, courtesy of a wonderful switch of play from the middle of the park out to the roving Richardson on the right flank. The winger then found a well-placed Mackay to test Rider in the travellers’ net, with the Kent club’s custodian unable to prevent the Rebel’s number nineteen from overtaking Amber Hazlewood as leading markswoman in a red (occasionally lilac) shirt.

Some fine build-up laid the foundations for a possible third not long afterwards, when a Hattie Rainey pass went from a central position to wide on the right again, releasing the rapid Richardson to, ultimately, find Mackay once more, with the forward teeing up Neve McEvaddy for a long-range piledriver which saw Rider pull off a terrific save.

Goalscorer nearly turned provider three-quarters of the way into the contest but neither Richardson nor Annie Gracey could apply the finishing  touch to a dangerous-looking delivery.

Almost instantly, the visiting Blues hit back via a neat move of their own, culminating in half-time substitute Kara Richardson forcing Woods to hold on.

Ten to go and another excellent long ball from Terry resulted in some equally impressive hold-up play by the recently-introduced Paige Baker-Carroll, providing Richardson with an opening that she couldn’t quite keep down.

Not over the line yet though, the home side were reminded of the threat carried by Aylesford when Bradding-Bulter’s corner eventually led to Kara Richardson drawing a one-handed stop out of Woods, at the (in)expense of another flag-kick.

Time was running out for the girls from the Garden of England and Armstrong was quick to pounce on Pritchard's pass to fellow replacement Megan Gates; although the final flourish from twenty yards failed to test Woods between the home posts.

Fittingly, Worthing’s brightly-clad netminder had the last word on proceedings, as she added to her collection of wonder saves by frustrating Sheridan with only a few short minutes of normal time to play.

That would, indeed, be that and three vital points stayed at the Sussex Transport Community Stadium to move the Rebels up to ninth in the table, ahead of another tough test at bottom-of-the-table and fellow Sussex side Eastbourne Borough next Sunday.

#1868. Barnsley's Patrick Kelly hoping Northern Ireland can soon be among Nations League big fish

Two years after winning their League C group to return to the second tier, Northern Ireland go into Tuesday’s match away to Hungary knowing they will be elevated to League A if they avoid defeat in Budapest.

The turnaround in Northern Ireland’s fortunes in this competition have been stark – prior to coming back up from League C they had just one win in 16 Nations League matches – but this young squad have taken huge steps forward since then.

Asked if he could have predicted Northern Ireland would be in this position with one game left, Barnsley midfielder Kelly told the Press Association: “I wouldn’t say I expected it but I wouldn’t have been shocked.

“I know we have a really good group and we fancy ourselves up against anyone and thankfully results have kind of gone our way and we’ve put ourselves in a really good position.”

The prospect of moving to the top tier of European football is a huge prize to put in front of this young side.

The 22-year-old Kelly’s most memorable moment in international football to date came with his fine goal in a 3-1 friendly defeat by France in June. Competitive fixtures against nations of that calibre would be the norm in League A.

“I think that’s a big incentive,” Kelly said. “It’ll just put us in a really good place if we can top the group, that’ll be a really strong finish to the campaign.

“Playing against teams like France, England, Spain, that would be good to test yourself at that level, to play against them more often and kind of see where we are.”

Northern Ireland will have to deal with two key suspensions in Budapest, with manager Michael O’Neill needing to watch from the sidelines after picking up a touchline ban, while striker Jamie Donley – who has travelled to Hungary – is also out after getting his second booking.

Kelly said he was not worried about O’Neill’s ban.

“Not much changes,” he said. “We’ll just have our game plan ready and go in and try to produce that,” he said. “We’ll just be ready to play the game.”

Donley’s suspension could offer a bigger role to Kelly with O’Neill weighing how to rejig his attacking options without the man who has led the line throughout this campaign.

“We’ve been working on it now,” Kelly said. “We’re not 100 per cent sure who is going to do that yet. Jamie will be a big miss for us but we’ve got a good squad and whoever’s called upon will be able to go in there and try to replicate what he’s been doing really well for us.”

#1867. Hassocks downed by Dockers for second time this season

Three times Hassocks have lost in the Southern Combination Premier Division so far this season. Two of those defeats have come at the hands of Newhaven.

The 2-1 scoreline at the Trafalgar Ground was the same as when the Dockers sailed back from Mid Sussex with all three points in August. The Robins must be delighted to see the back of Newhaven in the league.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

So often the scourge of Hassocks in the past, Lee Robinson scored both the Dockers goals in the space of seven second half minutes.

Lewis Finney pulled one back with 13 minutes remaining and although the Robins threw the kitchen sink at Newhaven, they were unable to find another way through.

The Dockers defence were outstanding and in particular ex-Hassocks centre back Matt Gunn, who deservedly picked up the host's man-of-the-match award afterwards.

Gunn was also a threat at the other end and had two chances to score twice himself inside the opening three minutes. He first saw a flicked header from a corner sensationally tipped around the post by Ed Cooper.

That resulted in another corner and although the Robins cleared this one, Newhaven were able to recycle possession and get a delivery from Ezra Roeg into the box. Gunn remained forward and met it with a powerful headed effort just over the bar.

Hassocks were unable to cope with the relentless tempo at which the Dockers had started. A situation summed up when Harry Reed and Tom Sekyere converged rapidly on Jack Troak to snare the ball from him.

The intense press got Tyler Capon in down the right flank for a cross which Cooper and Harvey Blake combined to clear in somewhat unorthodox, acrobatic style to prevent Robinson from having a tap-in.

Troak managed to lead an attack which finally broke the Robins out of their own half. His cross hung up into the middle was met by Dan Perry for a header just over.

Perry was making his Hassocks debut after signing from East Grinstead Town in midweek. The Hitman has netted 11 times this season for the Wasps and looks to be a quality addition.

Dan Turner then saw a shot from the edge of the box blocked by the nether regions of Elliott Bresciani. The defender putting his body on the line was an early sign of the sort of defending Newhaven would deploy to good effect to get them over the line in the second half.

With the Robins now a willing participant in the game, things began to ebb and flow from end-to-end. Capon was millimetres away from connecting with a Reed centre and Cooper did just enough to put off Sekyere into placing a one-on-one wide.

Perry looked the most likely source of goals for Hassocks. He drew a routine save from Jake Rhodes when heading a Harvey Blake cross on target.

Rhodes then pulled off a much more difficult reaction stop at close range when Big Alex Fair delivered and Perry stooped to direct a header across the Dockers goalkeeper.

Cooper saved well at his near post when Matt Feeney-Hill cut inside before Newhaven faded a little in the final 10 minutes of the half, probably because of the speed at which they played the previous 35.

As a result, Hassocks were on top in the period leading into the break. Finney saw a shot blocked by Gunn and some nifty footwork from Fair followed by a clever back heel teed up Omar Abdsami for a shot just a little too high.

The second half was a slow-burner in comparison to the first until Robinson fired the Dockers ahead on 63 minutes. Sekyere hooked a hopeful ball over the top of the Hassocks defence which the veteran forward showed a remarkable turn of pace to latch onto.

It carried Robinson clear of Turner and enabled him to curl a fine finish with his side foot around Cooper and into the far corner.

Newhaven doubled their lead with 70 on the clock after the Robins were unconvincing dealing with a corner. The delivery from Feeney-Hill was only half cleared to the edge of the box, allowing Ross Barclay to return an up-and-under into the area.

Gunn won a flick on and it found the unmarked Robinson, who had taken advantage of a slapdash Hassocks offside line to move front and centre of goal where he volleyed home unmarked.

Half-hearted appeals for the goal to be disallowed were easily dismissed. Robinson had stayed in a legal position, thanks in part to the Robins being completely out of shape.

Hassocks now had no choice but to lay siege on the Newhaven goal. Liam Benson came on as James Westlake changed formation and went with two up front.

The adjustment helped the Robins. Tall striker Jamie Wilkes put an awkward header wide and Devon Fender rattled the post with a good volley from inside the D.

An excellent move halved the deficit on 77 minutes. Abdsami was patient in waiting for a gap to appear into which he could play a forward pass.

When it came, his ball into the feet of Benson was superbly flicked around the corner by the substitute and into the path of Finney.

The finish from Finney was cool as you like as he picked out the far corner with aplomb to move onto double figures for the season.

Hassocks now had 13 minutes in which to try and find an equaliser. Unfortunately, their shooting from that point on did not match the calmness or precision with which Finney had pulled one back.

Finney came closest to providing a leveller on 88. Abdsami crossed and Perry directed a clever downwards header into the penalty box. The arriving Finney met it with a rasping volley which Rhodes somehow flung himself upwards to block.

Bresciani produced an overhead kick to clear the loose ball off the line and prevent Benson putting away the rebound. In a moment which summed the afternoon up really for Hassocks, that clearance gave another chance to Blake.

The Robins captain could only blaze so high as to pose more of a threat to Newhaven Fort all the way up the hill than the Dockers goal.

Other than the quality of the Finney finish, there was one other positive for the Robins to take home at least. Raging Joe Bull made his 300th senior appearance for the club, becoming the first Robin to pass the triple century landmark since Phil Gault a decade ago.

Hassocks: Cooper; Blake, D Turner, Hendy, Bull; Wilkes, Finney; Fair, Abdsami, Troak; Perry.

Subs: Fender, Benson, Budd (used), Croal, Brodie (unused).

#1866. Man United transfer news: Red Devils make Noussair Mazraoui 'decision' ahead of winter window

By Matt Law | 16 Nov 2026 10:40, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 10:42

Manchester United reportedly have no plans to allow Noussair Mazraoui to leave Old Trafford during the January transfer window.

There is currently speculation surrounding the Morocco international's future, with AC Milan and Juventus both believed to be keeping a close eye on the defender's situation.

Various clubs in Saudi Arabia are also thought to be interested in the 28-year-old.

However, according to the Daily Briefing, the 20-time English champions are not interested in selling the versatile defender in the middle of the campaign.

Mazraoui made the move to Man United from Bayern Munich in 2024, and he has made 85 appearances for the 20-time English champions.

The full-back has featured on eight occasions for the Red Devils this season, providing one assist, and he played the full 90 minutes of the team's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa in the Premier League before the international break.

It remains to be seen how heavily Mazraoui features under new Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino, who will officially begin work at Old Trafford on Thursday.

Mazraoui is currently with the Morocco squad in this international period, helping his national team to record a 5-1 win over Niger on November 13.

The defender is also due to be involved in the second clash with Niger on November 17 before heading back to Man United to prepare for Sunday's Premier League game against Liverpool.

Incoming Man United head coach Pochettino has big decisions to make when it comes to his back four for Sunday's Premier League game against Liverpool.

Luke Shaw could be available again after a period on the sidelines, while Lisandro Martinez is also free to return to the squad, having served a suspension against Villa.

Ayden Heaven, Leny Yoro, Matthijs de Ligt, Harry Maguire, Diogo Dalot and Patrick Dorgu are also options at the back, and it will be fascinating to see which defensive unit is selected by Pochettino this weekend.

Should Shaw again be ruled out, Mazraoui would have a strong chance of being named in the starting team at Anfield.

#1863. ‘Predictable, mutual, unfair’ - A brief history of Brighton’s sacked managers

So the current worst kept secret in football is out. Michael Carrick is no more at Old Trafford, it’s actually not United’s first rodeo in this footballing genre.

I recall being at the Amex on Easter Monday 2014, in the period of about 15 minutes I and four others in our party of ten that day received a forwarded text stating that David Moyes would be sacked as Manchester United manager the following morning, Tuesday 22nd April, and he was!

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Sackings are, unfortunately part and parcel of football. In my time following the Albion, we’ve had dismissals that have been predictable, justified, unfair and even a tad bizarre.

My first was Pat Saward in October 1973. I didn’t know much about, but in researching my book a couple of years ago, it was clear that once the ultra ambitious Albion chairman Mike Bamber got a sniff he might be able to rock the football world and bring Brian Clough to the Goldstone, dear old Pat was a dead man walking.

We then didn’t get another sacking for nearly a decade, and then it was all decided on the doorsteps of Sussex.

Mike Bailey had got the club it’s highest ever league finish, 13th in 81/82. But he was building from the back and at times the football wasn’t that exciting. Crowds dipped below the all important break even 15,000, and when fans were questioned by the lottery sellers on their weekly rounds, the word ‘boring’ was predominant and Bailey was out.

All these years later, I still believe the decision was a tad unfair and short sighted, but also one of those classic Brighton and Hove Albion sliding door moments.

Albion legend Steve Foster recently told me, whilst we probably wouldn’t have got to the 1983 Cup Final, we wouldn’t have got relegated and in time, Bailey could have turned us into a consistently top ten side, regularly challenging for Europe.

Bailey’s successor, Jimmy Melia, was almost in a footballing Sword of Damocles situation. Initially a caretaker boss, within a month the Albion embarked on an FA Cup campaign. With Bamber effectively waiting to wield the axe the Monday after the Albion were knocked out, but they weren’t. Melia, with his white dancing shoes took the Albion to Wembley but also rock bottom of the First Division and relegation!

Chris Cattlin was the next cab on the rank, his near three year tender, on a limited budget saw the Albion compete and again, like Bailey, given time, and funding, who knows what he could have achieved?

But he was unceremoniously dismissed at the end of the 85/86 season, but took the Albion to court for unfair dismissal, which resulted in his final victory at the club.

The returning Alan Mullery, another Goldstone legend, in the summer of 1986, was purely cosmetic. Replacing the popular Cattlin with the equally popular Mullery, saw a spike in season ticket sales, and not a lot more.

Mullery was a patsy, disgracefully treated when sacked in January 1987 for almost laughable reasons with the Albion in 13th.

A wretched run under new boss Barry Lloyd followed, with, as with the Division One exit in 1983, the Albion were relegated to the old Third Division in 22nd place in the division.

Yet we had to wait another nine years for another dismissal. Lloyd had left by mutual consent in December 1993, but in December 1996, with the cash strapped and soon to be homeless Albion in 92nd place in the Football League, Jimmy Case was unsurprisingly axed.

As was his successor, Steve Gritt, despite working a footballing miracle and keeping Albion in the league, he was gone in early 1998, again unjust, more about finance than football.

Exiled at Gillingham, crowds nowhere near break even, a massive shot in the arm was required, and that came in the shape of another returning legend (pattern forming) Brian Horton.

Jeff Wood, a genuinely nice guy, was in the wrong place at the wrong time Albion wise in 1999, as was Martin Hinshelwood in 2002.

Full disclosure, I’m in the privileged position to call a number of ex Albion bosses friends, and Mark McGhee is firmly in that catergory. His dismissal in September 2006, is another that sticks in the craw.

I do however still have a degree of sympathy in the bigger picture. At the time, Dick Knight, chasing our collective Falmer dream, was juggling all the balls whilst protecting his own.

Dean Wilkins, still in my opinion technically one of the best coaches the club has ever had, was both a safe pair of hands but a far cheaper option whilst the battle for the stadium went on, tellingly though however he has never worked as a manager since he departed the club in 2008.

I still believe that Mark McGhee would have mounted a promotion challenge to get us back in the Championship.

With the greatest respect in my opinion Albion wise Russel Slade still remains an irrelevance, only doing the job that Micky Adams would have done had he not resigned in February 2009.

Which brings us on to Gus Poyet, a footballing firework, it was great whilst it lasted, but it was what it was, and given off field working relationships, or lack of them, it was never going to last.

But to clarify Gus was not sacked live in the BBC, he was fully aware of the situation and his subsequent reaction was as genuine as American Wrestling!

But he still gave us some great memories, which will never be forgotten.

Chris Hughton’s sacking in 2019, was another exit, which leaves a bad taste. It could have been handled so much better. Like the Moyes text of 2014, I was told that Graham Potter was coming in 40 minutes before Hughton kicked off what was to be his final Albion game. Yet he was interviewed by Richie Reynolds on the pitch at the end about his hopes for the next season!

Potter, could and should have been sacked at least one or two occasions, but a crumb of comfort was the £20 million Chelsea gave us for his services, it truly is a funny old game.

So was Roberto De Zerbi sacked in May 2024, or merely his contract not renewed?

I still love his time as Albion manager, like Gus and others some amazing memories, but unfortunately there are boundaries and as soon as that microphone went under his nose in Rome with the apparent diatribe against Tony Bloom there was only going to be one outcome.

Which brings us around to Fab. Yes many, myself included, have embarked on the ‘Hurzeler Hokey Cokey’, but given the Albion’s current fortunes that’s well and truly parked.

You can never say never following the Albion but I think it’s a fairly safe bet there won’t be another Amex sacking anytime soon!

#1856. Belgium forward Romelu Lukaku announces shock retirement from international football

By Darren Plant | 16 Nov 2026 11:05

Belgium forward Romelu Lukaku has announced that he has retired from international football.

With 94 goals from 135 appearances, the Fenerbahce striker is Belgium's all-time record goalscorer.

Lukaku's most recent outing for Belgium was against France on November 5, the 33-year-old donning the captain's armband on that occasion.

However, Lukaku did not play in Belgium's last two fixtures, being ruled out versus Turkey last Thursday due to a hip injury and remaining as an unused substitute for Sunday's 4-1 victory over Italy.

On Monday morning, Lukaku took to social media to make the surprise revelation that he had called time on his international career.

A statement on Instagram read: "Over these 16 years, I gave everything for the national team…I experienced every emotion imaginable…

"I was lucky enough to play alongside extraordinary teammates, to whom I will always be grateful. I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches who pushed me to give my best and trusted me to help the team. It was a wonderful journey, and I cherished every moment.

"To the Belgian fans, thank you for all the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at 4 World Cups and 3 European Championships.

"I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was incredible. I enjoyed it immensely. I am grateful. Thank you."

Under both Rudi Garcia at the World Cup and Mark van Bommel across the six recent UEFA Nations League matches, Lukaku has not been viewed as a certain starter.

That is despite the former Chelsea, Everton and Manchester United forward scoring in four of his last seven outings for his country.

While Lukaku has not shed light on any potential issues behind the scenes, an assumption can be made that remaining as an unused substitute in two of the five games that he was available under Van Bommel has played its part.

At the age of 33, Lukaku had the opportunity to join a list of players who have reached 100 goals for their country. Only Cristiano Ronaldo, Lionel Messi and Ali Daei have achieved that feat.

Choosing to stay six goals short of the illustrious three figures feels an unusual choice on Lukaku's part, but it does not take away from ending his international career with 53 goals more than any other Belgian player in history.

He has been replaced by Frank, who has previously led Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur, and has now taken charge of a London club for the third time.

By Matt Law | 16 Nov 2026 11:52, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 11:55

Manchester United had reportedly considered Didier Deschamps as a replacement for Michael Carrick, but conversations with the Frenchman and his representatives over a move to Old Trafford 'did not go well'.

Carrick was sacked by Man United last week due to the team's struggles in the early months of the 2026-27 campaign, and Mauricio Pochettino has since been appointed at his replacement, with the Argentine due to officially take charge on November 18.

However, the report claims that the conversations 'did not go well'.

Man United allegedly believed that Deschamps was looking to gain leverage for a move to manage in Saudi Arabia.

Deschamps has been in charge of Monaco, Juventus and Marseille during his club management career, while he was France's boss between 2012 and 2026.

The former midfielder guided Monaco to success in the Coupe de la Ligue, in addition to overseeing a spot in the 2003-04 Champions League final.

Deschamps also lifted the Serie B title in 2006-07 while in charge of Juventus, in addition to Ligue 1, three Coupe de la Ligue trophies and two Trophee des Champions while at Marseille.

For France, Deschamps guided the team to the 2018 World Cup and 2020-21 UEFA Nations League trophies, in addition to helping the Blues reach the final of Euro 2016 and 2022 World Cup.

Deschamps is thought to be in line for a move to Saudi Arabia at some stage in the near future.

Antonio Conte, Julian Nagelsmann and Eddie Howe were also all linked with the role at Old Trafford before Pochettino's arrival was confirmed.

Pochettino will be aiming to make the perfect start to life at Man United when the Red Devils head to Liverpool in the Premier League this weekend.

He’s very confident about the future, stating he’s moving on to a ‘great opportunity’ and that the opportunity of working within the MSE ‘is as big as we want it to be’, as Sportico relayed. It’s a bold statement, but he’s no stranger to delivering.

#1848. Erling Haaland speaks out on Manchester City future as financial scandal rumbles on

Erling Haaland says he knows little or nothing about the financial scandal Manchester City are involved and is happy at the club, having signed a contract running until 2034.

In September Manchester City were found guilty of over 100 charges relating to breaches of Premier League financial rules.

City were found to have artificially inflated their financial position by over £900 million from 2009-18.

The club is now appealing those guilty verdict, with a hearing taking place in December and a decision on the appeal expected in early 2027.

If the appeal is unsuccessful than punishment is likely to be severe, with points deductions and fines likely and even expulsion from the Premier League a possibility.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Manchester City’s players have not said much about the situation and continue to compete, although three league defeats on the spin to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest may suggest the situation is taking its toll.

Haaland, though, says he has not even looked into the scandal much, pointing out that he was not at the club during the period of time that has been under investigation.

The 26-year-old scored in Norway’s 3-1 win over Wales on Saturday in Oslo and after successfully converting from the penalty spot, he successfully dodged the issue while speaking to TV2.

‘The investigation covered 2009 to 2018,’ he said. ‘In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2012, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don’t need the whole list…2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne’s first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

‘So this is a question I struggle to answer because it’s a legal battle…It’s a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with.

‘Am I supposed to answer that? I’m not really sure.’

The iconic striker then joked that these questions should be put to his compatriots that were at Manchester City during the time period in question.

Haaland dug out some names that only die hard Manchester City fans wil remember, saying: ‘There were quite a few Norwegians at the club during that period, I think.

‘Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen and Omar Elabdellaoui were there. Kjetil Haug was there too. I think there were a couple more but I can’t remember.

‘But it’s a difficult question to answer when I don’t really know that much about it. I assume the answers will come… I don’t know when. I haven’t read much about it.

‘To be completely honest, I’m focused on trying to perform for Manchester City. A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022 and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that says everything.’

Haaland stuck to his guns when asked about his thoughts on his future amid the ongoing appeal process.

‘I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said, I signed a long-term contract in 2024,’ he said. ‘I’d say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that.

‘I won’t say it myself, but look at the trophies I’ve won and how I’ve developed on and off the pitch. I’m standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we’re top of our group in Europe.

‘Things aren’t going so well for City in the league, but we’ll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can’t focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark.’

#1844. Declan Rice fires back at Graeme Souness after criticism from Liverpool legend

Declan Rice has fired back at Graeme Souness after stinging criticism, suggesting the Liverpool legend doesn’t understand how football has changed.

Rice is an integral player for England and Premier League champions Arsenal, widely recognised as one of the best midfielders in the world.

However, Souness has his own view and is not entirely sold on the talents of the 27-year-old, who he believes plays too deep to be considered a complete midfielder.

‘How many times do you see him as the last man with the ball? In the build-up, he’s last man,’ Souness said on Piers Morgan’s Football Uncensored. ‘He’s sitting between two centre-halves or between the centre-half and the full-back. He’s last man. A lot of the time, he doesn’t play in midfield.

‘It’s old man’s football. It’s cheating. An old man’s way of playing midfield. You get the ball under no pressure and you play it out to the full-back.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

He plays too deep to affect the game. I don’t think he’s got enough football. Let me tell you what he can do. He’s the best defensive midfielder in the country right now, he smells danger. But then again, he’s back there all the time.

In 323 Premier League outings for West Ham and Arsenal, Rice has scored 25 goals and provided 35 assists.

He is yet to scored in the top flight during the current campaign, but his five assists are more than any other player in the division.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Responding to the criticism from Souness, Rice said: ‘My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves. For a “centre back”, I think that’s not bad numbers. I’ve had a lot of assists, a lot of goals. To be a top-class centre back getting those numbers, I’m delighted with that!’

‘Look, Graeme’s got his opinion. I think he’s had his opinion since my West Ham days. I’ve seen his views. I can’t change his opinion. I can only do what I do, which is go on the pitch, perform, play well and block out the noise.’

Rice pointed out that there are different requirements placed in players in the modern game, using Harry Kane’s pitch-trotting exploits as an example.

‘If you speak about the positioning, the “old man’s football”, look at Harry Kane, for instance,’ he said. ‘We played him the other week [Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal] and he dropped next to the centre backs 20-30 times to pick up the ball.

‘The game is different now. It’s what the game demands, to get away from your man, to go into different areas to create overloads, to create two v ones, to progress the ball up the pitch. Football is way different. It’s changed a lot, and you’re always trying to look for tactical advantages.

‘In terms of me as a midfielder, I’m constantly watching clips with Mikel (Arteta). He’s constantly coaching me on the pitch. How I can progress the ball from deep, drop next to the goalkeeper, go to full back to get on the ball, to take the ball up the pitch.

‘So, I feel like we’re now seeing something totally different to what he would see, but in his time football was different. He was a top-class midfielder who won lots of stuff. There’s no argument against him. As a pundit, as a person, his career, you have to respect what he’s done.

‘I didn’t get to see him play, but obviously his accolades were top, and I’ve never got to meet him in person. If I did, there would be no disrespect. I’d shake his hand. I’d chat with him. It’s an opinion at the end of the day. It’s football.’

The Eagles appear to be moving quickly to replace Pierre Sage, who was sacked last Thursday after less than five months in charge.

However, former Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur boss Frank has now been identified as the leading candidate to take the reins at Selhurst Park, with ‘advanced talks’ held over the weekend.

The Athletic have since claimed that Palace are finalising an agreement to appoint Frank, who is expected to become the club’s new head coach.

Talks are said to be ongoing over Frank’s backroom staff and an official announcement of his arrival in South London is set to follow in due course.

All being well, Frank could potentially take charge of his first Crystal Palace game on Saturday when they travel to Coventry City in the Premier League.

If Frank is not appointed before the weekend, then the Dane could instead make his Palace debut in the Europa League when the Eagles play host to Real Sociedad on November 26.

The 53-year-old is set to return to management for the first time since he was sacked by Tottenham in February after only eight months in charge.

Frank won just 13 of his 38 matches with Spurs and left the club languishing in 16th place in the Premier League table, five points above the relegation zone.

He had previously enjoyed a successful seven-year spell as Brentford boss between 2018 and 2025, steering the Bees into the top flight and then establishing them as a competitive Premier League outfit, reaching a ninth-place finish in 2023.

In June, Frank stated that he had no intentions to take a new managerial position, but he now appears to be ready to return to the dugout and embark on a fresh challenge with Crystal Palace.

Frank will be tasked with lifting the Eagles off the foot of the Premier League table following a run of seven defeats in 10 games at the start of this season under Sage, conceding a division-high 24 goals in the process.

However, victory over Coventry this weekend could see Palace climb out of the relegation zone and up to 16th in the table if other results were to go their way.

Austin Trusty’s smart finish from a 10th-minute set-piece ensured Pochettino’s team were ahead at half-time before they ran riot after the break with Christian Pulisic able to net a brace either side of goals from Julian Hall, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun ahead of Tuesday’s second leg.

#1839. ‘No values, no spirit’ – Xavi blasts mentality of Netherlands squad

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Xavi attacked the mentality of his Netherlands squad after they fell to a humbling 5-0 loss against Germany in the Nations League on Monday.

Netherlands only needed a point to advance to the quarter-finals of the Nations League but suffered a heavy loss at the Olympiastadion that saw Germany win Group B.

Derry Scherhant's fine strike put Germany in front four minutes before half-time, and they added four goals in the space of 17 minutes during a frantic second-half period – Nico Schlotterbeck and Brajan Gruda scoring either side of Florian Wirtz's second goal.

The result was a bitter pill for Xavi to swallow having seen his team defeat Greece 7-0 on Friday, and he blasted his players for their performance.

"First of all, we have to say sorry for the supporters because we were not playing football – no values, no spirit, no anything," Xavi told NOS.

"As a coach, I cannot understand because we played an incredible game against Greece, with the spirit, values, intensity and passion. This was completely the opposite.

"Maybe because I'm new here, and I'm still trying to understand the spirit of the players – maybe it's a lack of mentality as well.

"I was talking to them, they talked as well, so I think it's good that we have had the communication and now we know the scenario.

"We have the capacity to do amazing things, but we did the complete opposite so it is a pity. I'm really disappointed, really sad because until [this match] I was really proud of the team, of the players – each one of them, but it was a shock for me as a coach.

"We're going to build something starting from now. I talked to the players honestly that we need to change the mentality and the values they have on the pitch even if we win, draw or lose. But it was impossible to complete [when] playing without values."

— OnsOranje (@OnsOranje) November 16, 2026

Xavi did not feel the absences of star duo Virgil van Dijk and Frenkie de Jong played a role in the result.

The Netherlands boss added: "It was 99% because of the values.

"It's embarrassing. We had the chances. We created things. We suffered because they played so well with the values that we wanted and that we had in the first five games.

"I'm trying to understand what happened, but it's difficult because three days ago we did an incredible game in terms of values and football-wise. But here the values were zero."

#1836. Spain 2-3 England: Thomas Tuchel’s side set new all-time winning record after “complete performance” in Nations League

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 12:57, Last updated: 16 Nov 2026 13:21

England have set a new all-time winning record after beating world champions Spain 3-2 in their final UEFA Nations League group fixture on Sunday.

The Three Lions knew that they had to beat the 2026 World Cup winners at Estadio Metropolitano on Madrid if they were to finish top of League A Group 3 on goal difference.

Thomas Tuchel’s side entered the half-time interval in front courtesy of a converted penalty from 2026 Ballon d’Or winner and England’s top goalscorer Harry Kane, who has set yet another scoring record.

Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White increased England’s lead with two goals in the space of just four minutes, putting the visitors firmly in control.

However, Elliot Anderson was sent off just six minutes after England’s third goal for a last-man pull-back on Lamine Yamal inside the penalty area, with Mikel Oyarzabal netting the resulting spot kick.

The momentum then shifted into Spain’s favour and substitute Nico Williams gave the hosts hope of a late comeback with a 75th-minute strike, but the Three Lions admirably dug deep to hold on for a crucial victory.

Victory for England means they have now won 10 consecutive away matches across all competitions for the first time in their history.

Success has also confirmed that England finish top of League A Group 3, progressing to the Nations League quarter-finals where they will face one of the runners-up in League A, with a guaranteed second leg at home.

Furthermore, England’s memorable night in Madrid saw them end Spain’s world-record 43-game unbeaten run spanning across almost three years.

After the match, Tuchel acknowledged that his team’s performance against La Roja was their best since he became England head coach in January 2025.

“Yes,” he told reporters. “Given the circumstances and the pressure and the quality and where we played and playing against the reigning world champions. That was a very complete performance and the best I’ve had so far.

“What a performance we put out there to be deservedly 3-0 up after 60 to 65 minutes. Of course the red card and the penalty changed the momentum and characteristic of the game. Thirty minutes [of defending] against Spain in Spain feels like three hours!

“This was, of course, a statement victory and the statement and significance of it was that it was deserved.

“The result followed the performance. It was on the highest level in terms of belief, team spirit, togetherness and it was on the highest level football-wise, on all aspects of the game.

“We did everything that needs to be done together – the deep buildup, the high press and attacking defensive phases.

England’s next match will be the first leg of their Nations League quarter-final tie, scheduled between March 25 and March 27 next year.

The Three Lions will discover their opponent when the draw is made on Friday at 11am UK time.

England cannot be drawn against Spain again, but they could face Group A1 runners-up Belgium, or one of three teams from Group A2 (Netherlands, Greece or Germany) or Group A4 (Portugal, Denmark or Norway).

The official quarter-final lineup will be confirmed after the final round of fixtures on Tuesday.
