#1833. Spain 2-3 England: Harry Kane equals 78-year Tom Finney scoring record in Nations League win

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 13:20

England captain Harry Kane has etched his name into the record books once again after scoring in Sunday’s 3-2 triumph over Spain in the UEFA Nations League.

The 2026 Ballon d’Or winner made his 127th international appearance at Estadio Metropolitano in Madrid, just three days after surpassing Peter Shilton as England’s most-capped player against Croatia.

On the stroke of half time, Kane fired England into a deserved half-time lead with a converted penalty after being felled by Spain defender Pau Cubarsi.

In doing so, England’s No.9 has now equalled an impressive scoring feat which had been unmatched since 1948.

Indeed, Kane has scored in each of his last seven international away matches dating back to June 2025, becoming the first Three Lions player to achieve this feat since legend Tom Finney between September 1946 and May 1948.

This record excludes neutral venues and therefore does not include the goals Kane scored at the 2026 World Cup where England finished third.

Kane’s away scoring streak began with goals in four successive World Cup qualifiers against Andorra, Serbia, Latvia and Albania, helping the Three Lions complete their qualification campaign with a perfect record.

The Bayern Munich striker has since netted in all three of his away matches with England in the Nations League against Czech Republic, Croatia and now Spain.

Kane has scored a total of 10 goals across those seven away games, while he has also extended his all-time scoring record with England to 93.

The last time Kane failed to make the net ripple for England at a non-neutral away venue came against Greece in November 2024 (3-0 Nations League win).

Kane will endeavour to surpass Finney outright and extend his scoring run on the road to eight games when England enter the Nations League quarter-finals in March 2027.

Reacting to England’s memorable win in Madrid, Kane told reporters: “I think that’s as big as it gets outside of a major tournament, for sure.

“We spoke before the Nations League campaign that we want to use these games to really improve, really stamp our identity on how we want to move going forward.

“No better game than Spain away after they’re unbeaten in 40-odd games to show that, and what a performance. Up until the red card it was dominant, clinical, high intensity and they couldn’t live with it.

“It was a shame [Elliot Anderson’s] red card happened because I think [the scoreline] could have been more and that’s been our mindset. That it doesn’t matter what the scoreline is – we go and we go and we go. You saw that out there tonight.

“In the end, we had to find a different way to win with the red card, obviously, and it was similar to a Mexico feeling where we’re digging deep.

“But when you can do both sides of the game like that it means you’re a very good team, so credit to everyone involved. It’s been a great campaign so far and we can end the year with our heads held high.”

Kane has scored in all six of England’s Nations League matches in the 2026-27 campaign, netting a competition-high eight goals in total to put him firmly in the frame to win the Golden Boot.

#1832. Klopp fell ‘head over heels in love’ with Germany squad

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Jurgen Klopp declared he fell in love with his Germany squad at first sight, as he heaped praise on their 5-0 destruction of the Netherlands in the Nations League on Monday.

The former Liverpool boss, appointed after the shock last-32 exit to Paraguay at the 2026 World Cup, assembled a huge 44-man squad for his first games in charge in September, splitting the group in two for their four matches.

Germany started slowly under Klopp and won just one of those fixtures – a 2-0 victory over Serbia – before the coach selected a standard 24-man squad for this international break which produced the goods.

After defeating Serbia 3-1 last Friday, they remarkably thrashed Xavi's Netherlands in Berlin to book their place in the Nations League quarter-finals.

"In the summer, you got the feeling that the new coach, which was me, had to get drunk to make the German national team look good. But I arrived and was head over heels in love – with 44 men," Klopp told ARD.

"Those who are here now are wonderful footballers, great characters. But the perception from the outside was different.

"We have a good idea, and thought if we can get these highly talented players moving, it could work well; then it won't be fun to play against us.

"And now everyone will go home with a smile and won't question the national team for at least three or four months.

"Instead they will think, 'This could be something special'."

Derry Scherhant curled his first international goal into the top corner just before half-time, before Florian Wirtz struck twice, with his goals coming either side of Nico Schlotterbeck's header.

Brajan Gruda impressed and he added to his pair of assists by rounding off the scoring with his second goal in as many international appearances.

"The game was extraordinary, also exceptionally difficult. We scored incredible goals, it was just insane," said Klopp.

"A fantastic football match, a magnificent experience. I wouldn't have dared to wish for something like this.

"This is a very special group at the moment.

"All problems have not been solved – that's nonsense, of course. But we have shown our potential. We have set the bar high for ourselves and we have to keep surpassing it."

#1826. Tottenham transfer news: Spurs ‘won’t panic buy’ in January as new striker pursuit is explained

By Oliver Thomas | 16 Nov 2026 13:41

Tottenham Hotspur are expected to accelerate their pursuit of a new striker during the January transfer window, according to a report.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side have struggled to convert chances so far this season, with only Sunderland (eight) and Nottingham Forest (nine) netting fewer goals than Spurs (10) in the Premier League after 10 games.

Spurs were unable to make the net ripple when they lost 1-0 at Leeds United before the international break, a result that ended a positive three-match winning run.

Dominic Solanke and summer signing Omar Marmoush have alternated leading the line under De Zerbi, but the pair have scored just three goals between them this season.

In fact, no Spurs player has scored more than two goals this term, with Solanke one of four men along with Conor Gallagher, Jan Paul van Hecke and Ben Davies who has netted multiple goals.

Spurs’ struggles in front of goal come at a time when Richarlison – the club’s top scorer with 11 PL goals last season – has been exiled from the senior squad after requesting to leave in the summer.

TEAMtalk reports that Bournemouth star Eli Junior Kroupi is a player ‘loved’ by De Zerbi, but his valuation between £80m and £100m could prove to be a major stumbling block for a club who spent in excess of £300m in the summer.

Spurs have since been on the lookout for alternative centre-forward options ahead of the New Year, with Freiburg frontman Igor Matanovic viewed as a possible target.

The 6ft 4in Croatia international has been in prolific form so far this season, scoring eight goals in 16 games across all competitions.

Journalist Ben Jacobs has revealed that Matanovic is indeed "one name" on Tottenham’s radar, but it remains to be seen whether they will push for the 23-year-old in January or wait until next summer.

Speaking on the Market Madness podcast, Jacobs said: “I think they could go for one [a striker] in January if the right target presents itself.

“It’s a shame how the Richarlison situation has panned out. Igor Matanovic is one name, as I exclusively revealed, that Tottenham like. They may look for something a little bit more short-term, like a loan. The same for Manchester United.

“If they can’t find the right target, or maybe someone with a bit more experience within the Premier League, then they can reassess in the summer.

“What they won’t want to do is necessarily go all in and panic buy in January for someone on a long-term contract, instead of just biding their time and waiting it out.”

Spurs could face competition from Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United for Matanovic, who is believed to be valued in the region of £50m.

Freiburg are in no rush to part ways with Matanovic, who remains a key player and is under contract at the Bundesliga club until 2029.

Re-signing striker Will Lankshear from Middlesbrough has also been mooted for Spurs, but the Championship club have allegedly slapped a £70m price tag on the 21-year-old, just months after signing him in the summer for a deal worth up to £20m.

#1825. Thomas Frank’s biggest Tottenham mistakes as Crystal Palace announce new manager

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

Thomas Frank succeeds Pierre Sage as Crystal Palace manager, signing a two-and-a-half-year deal with the south-east London club.

The Dane will be in the dugout for Palace’s trip to Coventry on Saturday, returning to management for the first time since leaving Tottenham in February.

Frank was on the Eagles’ shortlist to take over from Oliver Glasner this summer before they opted for Sage, and the former Spurs and Brentford boss is said to have been keen on a return to the Premier League.

After a difficult spell in north London, with the club sitting narrowly above the relegation zone when he left, Frank took time away from management to learn from leaders inside and outside football, as well as spending time with friends and family.

His disastrous stint at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium has inevitably left some scars, but Frank is still widely revered for his work in the west of the capital, where he got the Bees promoted to the Premier League, stabilising them as a top-flight club on one of the division’s lowest budgets.

Frank will undoubtedly have learnt some lessons from his seven-month spell at Spurs.

Here, Sam Tabuteau identifies the three biggest mishaps of Frank’s Tottenham tenure…

Part of what made Frank such an engaging character at Brentford was his ability to talk openly and honestly about the club’s culture, tactics and wider societal issues while maintaining an endearingly British sense of humour.

At times self-deprecating and sarcastic, Frank earned plenty of admirers for the way in which he humanised what can often be a cut-throat and emotionally vacant industry.

After nine years at Brentford, nearly seven as head coach, Frank had earned the luxury of being able to talk so candidly. He was comfortable in his surroundings, and safe in the knowledge that Brentford had not sacked a manager since 2015.

However, at Tottenham, he was starting from scratch at a club whose ambitions don’t leave much room for home truths.

Coming off the back of their Europa League triumph, Spurs supporters wanted to hear how the club was going to push forward.

Yet in his first press conference as Spurs manager, Frank joked that if there was one thing he could promise, it was that they would lose games.

Frank appointed new Crystal Palace manager

Frank’s first words as Palace manager as former Spurs boss appointed

Arteta facing new Arsenal dilemma after inevitable Gyokeres goals

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

His ill-timed quip did not go down well, regardless of the spirit in which it was intended, and from that point on Frank was fighting a losing battle to convince supporters he understood the culture of the club.

Losing supporters after tame Chelsea defeat

Given how it ended, Frank’s tenure started surprisingly positively, with Tottenham third in the Premier League table after nine games.

The mood quickly changed, though, after a dispiriting 1-0 home defeat to London rivals Chelsea, in which Spurs managed just one shot on target.

Frank’s pragmatic style worked well at Brentford because they had one of the most efficient frontlines in the division and were not expected to dominate possession.

At Spurs, however, Frank’s risk-averse style combined with an attacking unit missing Dejan Kulusevski and James Maddison meant they relied heavily on set-piece goals and struggled to create chances in open play.

Frank’s inability to evolve his style, coupled with Spurs’ shortcomings in attack, culminated in a performance against Chelsea that left many supporters disillusioned and would come to symbolise his time in charge.

Another example of Frank’s naivety came during January’s stoppage-time defeat to Bournemouth, when the 53-year-old was pictured pre-match walking around the pitch at the Vitality Stadium with an Arsenal-branded coffee cup.

Seemingly none the wiser, Frank stood with the cup in hand while some staff members could not hide their shock, and the resulting pictures went viral as Spurs slumped to an excruciating defeat.

After the game, Frank’s blunder took centre stage, and his mystified reaction just about summed up the growing rift between him and Spurs’ supporters.

While Spurs fans vented their anger and embarrassment online and in the stands, Frank could not begin to understand how an innocent mistake could be blown so far out of proportion.

From that point on, it was clear that the narrative was quickly beginning to slip from Frank’s grasp and Spurs would lose their next five league games before he was relieved of his duties.

England ended Spain’s incredible 43-match unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory in Madrid on Sunday evening.

The hard-fought win means England, already through to the quarter-finals of the Nations League, finish top of their group ahead of World Cup holders Spain.

#1823. What is the 3pm blackout? Could Premier League rule be scrapped after Andy Burnham comments?

Prime Minister Andy Burnham says he would “urge caution” on scrapping the Saturday 3pm blackout, and called for broadcasters to be mindful of the impact on fans caused by changes to kick-off times.

The ban on broadcasting live matches between 2.45pm and 5.15pm on Saturdays was introduced in the 1960s but it could be dropped for the next set of Premier League, EFL and Scottish Professional Football League (SPFL) rights cycles from 2029-30.

The purpose of the blackout has been to protect live attendance at matches, amid fears crowds would be affected, especially in lower league or non-league football, if top-flight matches were available to watch on television or streaming services.

Burnham said any decision to remove the ban would require careful thought about the consequences.

“I would urge a bit of caution on it (the blackout), because it does protect the income of lower-league clubs,” he said.

“If you have effectively wall-to-wall Premier League football at any time, it takes away perhaps the incentive to go and watch the football league or non-league.

“So I think it has to be considered carefully. I’m not going to take the pure consumer view here. I’ll take the health-of-football approach to this particular issue.

“I would first of all want to protect the football pyramid before I agree to saying ‘let’s have even more live football’.

“I think it’s about protecting the experience with the paying supporter, protecting the football pyramid. Those issues matter to me, first of all.”

The trend in television rights has been to offer more matches in order to keep revenues up – the current Premier League deal includes 270 live matches compared to 200 in the previous one for example.

The logical conclusion of that trend is for all matches to be made available live, and the SPFL’s tender for its next set of rights is reported to offer the chance to do just that.

The blackout is enforced by Article 48 of UEFA’s statutes, which the Football Association and the Scottish Football Association choose to impose.

It applies when 50 per cent or more of matches in the top two divisions are due to be played simultaneously.

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters told talkSPORT in August that English football was leaning towards a blackout but added: “It’s not just us involved in the decision about Article 48. It’s us, the EFL and the FA.

“”We’ve got to take that decision at some point in the future about whether things are going to change.

“It’s not a decision for now. It’s a decision we’ve got to make before the next set of domestic processes that the EFL and the Premier League are going to do.

“I’d say in about 18 months’ time we’ll come back to that decision about whether Article 48 should remain or not.”

Burnham was also asked if broadcasters needed to be more mindful of the disruption caused to fans by the scheduling of matches for live broadcast.

“It doesn’t give any regard, actually, as far as I can see, to travelling supporters,” he said.

“Monday night games, you know, people in the north-east coming to the north-west, it’s not fair, the way that is done, or very early kick-offs on Saturday, very difficult for people to get there. So on that, I agree (with the need to be more mindful).

#1822. Frank vows to turn Crystal Palace’s fortunes around after replacing Sage

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Thomas Frank described Crystal Palace as an "iconic club" and vowed to turn their fortunes around after being announced as the Eagles' new manager.

Frank was appointed as Pierre Sage's successor on Monday after the Frenchman was dismissed during the international break with Palace at the bottom of the Premier League.

The 53-year-old is back in management nine months on from his tumultuous stint with Tottenham, which ended with the club sitting just outside the relegation zone.

Frank, who has penned a deal through to the end of the 2028-29 season, had been linked with the Palace job in the summer after Oliver Glasner left for Nottingham Forest.

It was also reported that Fulham were interested in his services, only to opt for Alvaro Arbeloa, while Sage was preferred to take the reins at Palace.

Frank Lampard, Sean Dyche, Vitor Pereira, Kim Hellberg, Vitor Matos, Tony Popovic and Ole Werner were all viewed as potential candidates to replace Sage.

But Palace have chosen to go with Frank, who will be the third manager to take charge of three different London clubs in the Premier League after Alan Pardew (Charlton Athletic, Crystal Palace, West Ham) and Harry Redknapp (Queens Park Rangers, Spurs, West Ham).

"It's an honour to sit here and be in charge of this fantastic football club. I'm really, really looking forward to it," Frank told Palace's official website.

"Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League.

"I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place, and I'm really looking forward to meeting them."

First day complete Thomas Frank is in the building. https://t.co/6XDUexHQT7

— Crystal Palace F.C. (@CPFC) November 16, 2026

Frank impressed during a seven-year stint with Brentford, winning 41.8% of his 317 games in charge of the Bees (W132 D77 L108).

However, he was unable to replicate that with Spurs, averaging just 1.12 points per game with the club in the Premier League (29 points in 26 games) and accumulating a win rate of 34.2% (P38 W13 D11 L14).

Despite Frank's struggles at Spurs, Palace chairman Steve Parish believes his experience of managing in the Premier League made him a "perfect fit" for the Eagles.

"I'm delighted to be able to welcome Thomas to Crystal Palace," Parish said.

"He has a proven track record of both creating winning teams and improving players, making him the perfect fit for our club.

"I'm confident Thomas' extensive experience in the Premier League will help us achieve our goals for the rest of the season."

Frank will lead Palace out for the first time this Saturday in a clash against Lampard's Coventry City.

#1821. Thomas Frank appointed new Crystal Palace manager on two-and-a-half year deal

Thomas Frank has been confirmed as Crystal Palace’s new manager, with the Dane in post for the trip to Coventry this weekend.

He replaces Pierre Sage, who was sacked last week with Palace bottom of ther Premier League table.

Frank, who has been out of work since leaving Tottenham in February, was on Palace’s shortlist over the summer as they looked for a replacement for Oliver Glasner.

The Eagles ultimately agreed a three-year deal with Sage, but a disastrous start to the season saw the Frenchman relieved of his duties on Thursday.

The Dane has penned a two and a half year contract with the south Londoners, with club chairman Steve Parish hailing his “proven track record”.

“I’m delighted to be able to welcome Thomas to Crystal Palace,” Parish said in the club announcement.

“He has a proven track record of both creating winning teams and improving players, making him the perfect fit for our club.

“I’m confident Thomas’ extensive experience in the Premier League will help us achieve our goals for the rest of the season.”

In his first words as Palace boss, Frank called his new side an “iconic club”.

"It's an honour to sit here and be in charge of this fantastic club. I'm really, really looking forward to it.

"Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League. I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place, and I'm really looking forward to meeting them.”

Frank endured a difficult spell at Spurs, who had been dragged into a relegation battle by the time he was sacked, but there remains a good deal of appreciation for his work at Brentford.

During his time in west London, Frank earned promotion to the Premier League before stabilising Brentford as a top-flight club and getting them challenging for Europe on one of the smallest budgets in the division.

Frank’s immediate task will be to drag Palace out of the relegation zone, starting with back-to-back fixtures against newly promoted Coventry and Hull.

#1820. Declan Rice says England ‘knew’ they would beat World Cup holders Spain

Declan Rice says the England squad ‘knew’ they would beat World Cup holders Spain in their final Nations League group game.

England earned top spot in their Nations League group and ended Spain’s extraordinary 43-game unbeaten run with a thrilling 3-2 win in Madrid.

Thomas Tuchel’s side scored three goals in 12 minutes either side of half-time to stun Spain before withstanding a late siege to seal their finest win under the German boss.

Harry Kane took his international tally to 93 goals with a penalty on the stroke of half-time as England deservedly ended the opening 45 minutes ahead.

Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White then scored twice in the space of four minutes to open up a commanding 3-0 lead over the shell-shocked Spaniards.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But Elliot Anderson’s red card on 63 minutes and Mikel Oyarzabal’s subsequent penalty offered Spain a route back into a match they looked out of.

England fans feared a collapse similar to the one the team suffered in last summer’s World Cup semi-final against Argentina when Nico Williams scored Spain’s second with 20 minutes remaining.

But this time England kept their opponents at bay with some resolute defending and two superb saves from goalkeeper James Trafford.

Rice was full of praise for his teammates after the Nations League win and said he ‘knew’ England would beat the world champions in their own backyard.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘We knew we were going to beat them tonight,’ Rice told ITV. ‘The message from the manager after the Croatia game has been so positive.

"We knew we were going to beat them tonight!"Declan Rice after England's win over Spain in Madrid 🇪🇸🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 pic.twitter.com/dbNiMi74od

‘Our first ten minutes were probably the best we’ve played. It was pressure, pressure, pressure – we could have had two or three.

‘If we don’t go down to ten men, we see more of the ball, we start to see them jump more, we start to see more space, and we start to see our attacking players thrive like they were doing in the second half.

‘With ten men for half an hour, winning 3-2 against that team is massive. It’s a massive win. Credit to everyone.

‘When they got the second, you might have thought that it was going to go the other way with the amount of pressure they were putting on, but that resilience.

‘Keep emptying the tank, doing anything for this badge, for this team, for our players, for the manager.’

Meanwhile, Tuchel hailed England’s ‘brilliant performance’ after they beat a side who last lost in regulation play in March 2024.

‘Brilliant performance. Well deserved win,’ he said. ‘Overall we were the better team. Fantastic performance from start to finish.

‘It was a long 30 minutes after the red card but I don’t want to focus on that. There were so many positive things in the first 60 minutes.

‘Complete performance. We brought everything to the table. We were brave. Spirit wise, energy wise and also football quality was highest level.

‘We deserved it. We focused on our performance and attitude. I can’t praise the team high enough for what they put out there.’

By Darren Plant | 16 Nov 2026 13:55

Jorginho has revealed that Chelsea's squad disagreed with BlueCo's decision to sack Thomas Tuchel in 2022.

Tuchel is currently receiving widespread plaudits after his England team ended Spain's 43-game undefeated streak on Sunday evening.

England stormed into a three-goal lead inside an hour, before an Elliot Anderson red card contributed to the Three Lions having to see out a nervy end to the contest in Madrid.

The result has helped Tuchel rebuild his reputation in big games, but the German will forever regarded as a Chelsea legend after the club's Champions League triumph in 2021.

However, 15 months on from that success in Porto, Tuchel was sacked by Chelsea's new owners BlueCo.

Speaking on the 'Obi One Podcast' hosted by former Blues midfielder John Obi Mikel, Jorginho acknowledged that he and his teammates were left stunned by the decision.

Asked to describe the reaction of Chelsea's first-team squad and himself, Jorginho replied: "What?".

"Like this. We were like 'we didn't expect it'. We were not having the best results at that moment, but us, it was not the moment.

At the start of the 2022-23 campaign, Chelsea collected 10 points from their opening six matches in the Premier League.

However, it was a 1-0 defeat away in Dinamo Zagreb that led to Tuchel being sacked by BlueCo on the following morning.

BlueCo had only just signed known Tuchel favourite Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang to become the club's new number nine.

Since that decision on September 7, 2022, it has since been suggested that BlueCo wanted to appoint their own head coach, the indication being that they did not want a manager chosen by predecessor Roman Abramovich to remain at the helm if they were not fully aligned in their relationship and club strategy.

Newcastle United’s Lewis Hall was a top target during the summer transfer window, but United did not act on that interest, with the former Chelsea defender penning a new deal on Tyneside instead.

Now, the Press Association reports that the Magpies will not entertain any offers for the England international in the upcoming January transfer window.

He has established himself as Thomas Tuchel’s first-choice left-back in recent months, and he impressed against Lamine Yamal in the Three Lions’ shock 3-2 win over Spain in the Nations League on Sunday.

It is thought that Newcastle are braced for more transfer interest in their 22-year-old, who signed for the north-east club in 2023, costing them £35million.

It is believed that they have no intention of selling him halfway through the campaign, having lost Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon and Alexander Isak in the space of two summer transfer windows.

#1816. Canada can ‘do really good things’ in Nations League Finals after Guatemala win

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Mauro Biello is confident that Canada can "do really good things" after they qualified for the CONCACAF Nations League Finals with a 4-1 victory over Guatemala on Monday.

Canada took a 3-2 lead into the second leg at BMO Field but were without Alphonso Davies, who suffered a muscular issue in the opening match and joined the likes of Cyle Larin, Stephen Eustaquio and Ismael Kone on the injury list.

Despite a strong start from the hosts, Oscar Santis drew Guatemala level on aggregate when he showed great composure on the edge of the six-yard box in the 34th minute.

But Jonathan David equalised from the spot five minutes later and Tani Oluwaseyi made it two on the stroke of half-time, putting Canada back in control of the tie.

Tajon Buchanan scored his first international goal since last year's Gold Cup after the restart and Oluwaseyi nodded in his second before the hour mark to complete a 7-3 aggregate victory.

Biello, who stood in for the suspended head coach Jesse Marsch, suggested Canada's injury problems could help spur them to a first trophy since winning the 2000 Gold Cup by increasing the competition in the squad.

"These are tough games. It was a tough game also in Guatemala, and you saw it here: you're in total control of the game, and then it's 1-0 to them," said Biello.

"Getting these injuries is not fun. You're losing key guys, but at the same time, we're expanding this pool of players.

"Guys are getting opportunities, and guys are taking their moments.

"It's a good team, right? If we're able to get these guys all revving their engines, we're going to be able to do really good things."

Manchester United’s alternative targets to Mauricio Pochettino have been revealed.

They turned to the former Tottenham and Chelsea boss after it became clear that he had a £7.5million release clause in his contract with US Soccer as head coach of the United States’ men’s side.

Now, The Athletic has reported the six other names that United’s hierarchy considered before landing the Argentine, who will take charge of his new club on Wednesday.

It is believed that the Red Devils explored Unai Emery’s availability, but the Aston Villa manager’s level of authority at his current club was understood to be too difficult to match.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann, formerly of Newcastle and Bayern Munich respectively, were publicly-known candidates for United, but the former was decided against without any further consideration, while the latter’s lack of Premier League experience ultimately went against him. The Athletic claims that United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe held a personal interest in another ex-Chelsea and Tottenham figure, Antonio Conte, but the Italian’s desired level of control over club proceedings was believed to be ‘not the right fit’.

#1814. Luis de la Fuente singles out ‘fantastic’ England star after Spain defeat

Luis de la Fuente reserved special praise for James Trafford following Spain’s 3-2 defeat to England, hailing the goalkeeper’s ‘fantastic’ display in Madrid.

England produced arguably their finest all-round performance under Thomas Tuchel in Sunday’s Nations League classic to land a hefty psychological blow on the reigning world and European champions.

The Three Lions flew out of the blocks from minute one and were duly rewarded for their efforts as captain Harry Kane converted from the spot to break the deadlock on the stroke of half-time.

Goals from Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White increased the deficit after the restart, with Spain all at sea before Elliot Anderson’s sending off handed the hosts a lifeline.

Mikel Oyarzabal scored with the resulting penalty before Nico Williams finished off a flowing Spanish move to set up a tense final 15 minutes at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano Stadium.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But ten-man England managed to keep La Roja at bay thanks largely to an inspired Trafford, who was selected over Jordan Pickford and repaid Tuchel’s faith with a series of stunning late stops to help preserve the visitors’ narrow advantage

Trafford’s double save to keep out Fermin Lopez and Aymeric Laporte earned the Leeds United keeper immediate high fives and adulation from his team-mates.

The result brought Spain’s incredible 43-match unbeaten streak to a halt and ensured England finished top of their Nations League group having picked up 15 from a possible 18 points.

‘Positives? There are a lot of positives to find here. It’s very difficult to get here, to achieve the numbers that we’ve achieved,’ Spain boss De La Fuente said when asked about Spain’s run being brought to an end.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘It’s something historical that we’ve done. We’ve been champions of the Nations League, the Euros, the World Cup, everything is positive.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘But we know how to win and we know how to lose. And we have to say that we faced a rival that we managed to beat in the past but I have to say that they were the better team in the first 30 minutes.

‘I had a feeling we could get there when they went one man down but I’m really proud of this team, their hunger, their eagerness.

‘I’m convinced that the best is yet to come for this team.’

De la Fuente made four second-half substitutions as they looked to claw their way back into the contest, with Fermin Lopez, Nico Williams, Pedri and Dean Huijsen all sent on in the Spanish capital.

But the home team were thwarted by Trafford’s heroics in the closing stages – and De la Fuente took the opportunity to applaud the ‘keeper’s outstanding showing.

‘What we wanted to do with the substitutions was try to go all out, try to generate more chances,’ he explained.

‘We did generate some chances but England’s goalkeeper has produced a fantastic performance and stopped two or three potential goals in the last ten or 15 minutes.

‘In any case, there were many alternatives but again, I want to say how fantastic England were on the night.’

Asked what he and Tuchel had discussed shortly after the final whistle, De La Fuente replied: ‘We just spoke for a few seconds about what happened this week and we just wanted to clarify things.

‘I have no problem with him at all, all I have is admiration and respect.

‘As for the dressing room, when you are not used to losing, you look at eachother and ask, “What happened here?”, so what did I tell my players? I told them that we haven’t lost for three years and we’ve won all the important tournaments.

‘All I wanted to do was say how proud I am of them because of this and it’s a shame we don’t have another game coming up, we have to wait until March.’

The Spain head coach added: ‘We’ll surely come back in March with renewed energy, thinking about the Nations League final.

‘We’re going to try to get there, knowing difficult it is to get there and win a competition like this.

‘But the spirit, the intention, the ambition are all there.’

#1812. Thomas Frank's Crystal Palace in-tray: Three big issues new Eagles boss must solve to avoid relegation

By Lewis Blain | 16 Nov 2026 15:28

Crystal Palace are closing in on the appointment of Thomas Frank as their new head coach, according to The Athletic, with the former Tottenham Hotspur and Brentford boss expected to replace Pierre Sage at Selhurst Park.

The 53-year-old faces an enormous challenge after Palace collected just seven points from their opening 10 Premier League matches, leaving them at the foot of the table. He has only a handful of days to work with his new squad before Saturday's trip to Coventry City, making an immediate improvement essential.

Frank has plenty of rebuilding to do after his difficult spell in north London, but his successful seven-year stint at Brentford offers encouragement.

Sports Mole looks at three priorities that should dominate his in-tray in the first few months.

Frank's most urgent task will be to address a defence that has conceded 24 goals in just ten Premier League matches, the worst record in the division. Palace have also shipped eight goals from set pieces, including four during their current run of four consecutive defeats.

It is a problem that predates Sage's arrival, having also troubled Oliver Glasner, but Frank has a reputation for organising competitive sides and could bring some much-needed structure. At Brentford, he alternated between a 3-5-2 and 4-3-3, with the former potentially straightforward to implement given Palace's familiarity with a back three.

However, the personnel available to him remain a concern. Palace did not adequately replace Maxence Lacroix and Marc Guehi, while summer arrivals Takehiro Tomiyasu, Axel Disasi and 18-year-old Honest Ahanor have not necessarily provided the defensive stability required.

Disasi is a particularly interesting case. The Chelsea loanee has an opportunity to establish himself as a key figure, but Frank must decide whether he is the right partner for the existing defensive options or whether further recruitment is required.

Frank's Brentford teams were also particularly dangerous from dead-ball situations, ranking among the Premier League's best for set-piece expected goals during his time there. Bringing that same attention to detail to both boxes could make an immediate difference.

Adam Wharton's decline in influence has been another major frustration for Palace. Only a few months ago, the midfielder was attracting reported interest from Chelsea, Manchester City and Liverpool, having established himself as one of the most exciting young English players in the Premier League.

Now, the noise surrounding his future has quietened considerably. Wharton missed out on England's 2026 World Cup squad and has struggled to reproduce the performances that previously made him so highly rated.

His average performance rating has dropped from fourth-best among Palace players in 2025-26 to seventh this season, with his contribution in possession and defensive work both coming under scrutiny.

Some of those difficulties appear connected to the unfamiliar responsibilities he has been given under Sage. Wharton has struggled to track runners and protect the space in front of the defence, and while not known for his attacking prowess, his influence in transition and in the final third has waned, registering fewer accurate long balls and key passes per 90 in the Premier League.

Frank must find a role that allows the 22-year-old to dictate games without leaving him exposed defensively. Restoring Wharton's confidence and getting him closer to his previous level would represent a significant boost, both for Palace's survival hopes and his longer-term development.

Palace's problems in front of goal are not quite as severe as their defensive shortcomings, but Frank will need to address the uncertainty surrounding his centre-forward options.

Jean-Philippe Mateta wanted to leave during the summer and is approaching the final months of his contract, while an injury has already disrupted his campaign. The Frenchman has yet to score in the Premier League this season and has accumulated more red cards than goals, leaving his future increasingly uncertain.

Jorgen Strand Larsen has also struggled to convince since arriving, managing just one goal in eight league appearances. His record of 19 goals in 79 top-flight outings hardly suggests he is ready to become a reliable long-term replacement for Mateta.

Frank may therefore need to look beyond Selhurst Park when the January window opens. A reunion with Richarlison, who looks to be available from ex-club Spurs, is one possibility worth considering, particularly given the Brazilian's previous experience under the Dane.

Palace spent heavily on 11 summer arrivals, so chairman Steve Parish may be reluctant to sanction another significant recruitment drive. Nevertheless, losing Mateta without securing a dependable replacement would leave Frank with a major problem.

With Palace already facing a fight to climb away from the bottom of the table, Frank cannot afford to wait until January to make improvements.

Defensive organisation, Wharton's revival and a reliable goalscorer represent three clear priorities if he is to turn a troubled season around.

#1811. Thomas Tuchel speaks out on James Trafford vs Jordan Pickford battle for England spot

Thomas Tuchel insists that England do not have a number one, after James Trafford made a brilliant case to be first choice goalkeeper in the win over Spain.

Trafford played the full game as the Three Lions pulled off a memorable 3-2 Nations League win over the world champions in Madrid.

It was a stunning first hour from Tuchel’s side and the visitors were 3-0 up on 57 minutes thanks to goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

Things started to unravel a bit from there as Elliot Anderson was shown a straight red card and Mikel Oyarzabal converted from the penalty spot.

Nico Williams then made it a very nervy climax for England as he scored on 75 minutes and the hosts pushed for an equaliser.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Trafford helped his team stand firm, though, including making a tremendous double save late on.

Everton’s Jordan Pickford has been first choice goalkeeper since 2018, winning 94 caps, but his place is now in doubt thanks to the emergence of Trafford.

James Trafford last-gasp double save 🤯🤯#UNLSaves | @Betano_PT pic.twitter.com/K3Rn995OEE

Tuchel was not ready to declare either stopper his number one, but was clearly very impressed by the Leeds United star.

‘There’s no number one,’ said the England boss. ‘It’s a good double save. That’s what we wanted. He had a brilliant match. It only works if you’re top from number one to 11.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Tuchel continued on Trafford: ‘Very good. That’s his job, to close the gap. We want competition in all positions. We need to see Trafford in high-pressure moments.

‘The obvious save, where he deserves full credit, is the double save at the very end. Absolutely brilliant.’

The German has also liked what he has seen from Trafford on the ball, saying: ‘There was a lot to do in the deep build-up as well, which he did very, very well, with everyone around him.

‘Never lose the concentration, never lose the focus, never lose the vision where to find the free men to overcome the press and put the game to the opponent’s half.

‘With everyone else, he was part of a fantastic team performance.’

At 24 years old, Trafford is eight years younger than Pickford and looks to be his successor, even if he has not entirely displaced him just yet.

The win in Spain meant England topped their Nations League group and will play a runner-up from another group in the quarter-finals of the competition.

Groups A2 and A4 come to an end on Monday and Tuesday respectively, which is when we will learn England’s possible opponents for Friday’s draw.

Belgium have already secured second place in group A1, so they are a possible opponent for the Three Lions in the quarter-finals that are played in March next year.

His side won 6-0 in their first match, and he will take charge of his final game on Tuesday before flying over to Manchester on Wednesday morning.

The Athletic reports that Pochettino’s assistants have already made their way over to England to begin work, with Toni Jimenez, Jesus Perez and his son Sebastiano Pochettino all beginning their new jobs at Carrington early.

Miguel D’Agostino, Pochettino’s long-serving assistant manager, has remained with the USMNT head coach for the second leg against Haiti in Cincinnati, but he is also expected to join his colleague at United later this week.

Pochettino’s first game in charge will come this Sunday, when he oversees his new side against Liverpool at Anfield.

#1809. Man Utd told Chelsea star would be ‘good signing’ for Mauricio Pochettino

Mikael Silvestre has encouraged Manchester United to explore a move for Estevao – but doubts the forward could be coaxed to the Theatre of Dreams as he appears intent on ‘fighting for his place’ at Chelsea.

United spent in the region of £160million on new signings in the summer, with club chiefs showing they were prepared to back Michael Carrick following an impressive third-place finish.

But any optimism that had grown amongst the fanbase in the back-end of last season rapidly faded as a 2-0 defeat away to Chelsea last month extended the Red Devils’ miserable winless run to nine matches in all competitions.

A stunning comeback victory over Roma followed by a 4-4 thriller at home to Aston Villa in the Premier League were ultimately not enough to save Carrick, who was relieved of his duties last Thursday.

Former Tottenham and Chelsea head coach Mauricio Pochettino was subsequently announced as Carrick’s successor, with the Argentine officially vacating his position with the United States national team to start life in the role later this week.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Naturally, attentions have quickly turned towards the January transfer window, when United will be expected to splash the cash in the hope of boosting their prospects for the second half of the campaign.

United chiefs are set to resurrect their pursuit of a left-back as a priority to provide support for Luke Shaw after missing out on Newcastle’s Lewis Hall in the summer.

It’s understood the Old Trafford giants will also be in the market for attacking reinforcements on the back of a desperately disappointing start to the season for the likes of Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and Benjamin Sesko.

According to Silvestre, Chelsea winger Estevao could represent a ‘good signing’ for United, with the Brazilian having made just one start in the Premier League under Xabi Alonso.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

That start happened to come against United, though, and the 19-year-old was widely praised for his performance as goals from Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer proved decisive at Stamford Bridge.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘Well, Estevao played against United for Chelsea, and I think he’s shown why he should feature more,’ Silvestre told Betarades.gr.

‘It looks like he’s going to fight for his place in the team, so I don’t anticipate United making a move for him.

‘But he’s a good player for sure. He’s playing for the national team of Brazil, and I like his style. If he were available, he would be a good signing for United.’

Asked why Newcastle and England star Hall may ‘make sense’ for United at left-back, Silvestre replied: ‘Lewis Hall had an impressive season with Newcastle, and he’s been on the club’s radar for sure.

‘The club made an attempt to sign him and other fullbacks, but couldn’t get it done.

‘They now have to rely on Luke Shaw, Diego Dalot, on Noussair Mazraoui, and on Patrick Dorgu, who has also been injured for quite some time. So that’s not been helpful either.’

Another high-profile name heavily linked with United in recent weeks has been Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who has scored five goals in his opening nine appearances for Leeds this term.

But Silvestre, who won five Premier League titles with the Red Devils, believes the England striker would only be brought in as a stop-gap for his former club up front.

‘I think Dominic Calvert-Lewin would be a stop-gap,’ the ex-United and France defender explained.

‘I don’t think it’s a long-term. He doesn’t belong in a Manchester United squad. So I don’t know where this is coming from.

‘Yes, you need to have a look around for strikers because of the Sesko situation with his injury, and we are short in that department, but I wouldn’t consider Calvert-Lewin as an option.’

All eyes will be on Anfield on Sunday when Pochettino takes charge of United for the first time against bitter rivals Liverpool.

Pochettino takes over the reins from Carrick with the club languishing down in 18th place in the Premier League, just point better off than rock-bottom Crystal Palace.

#1808. Prediction: Bayern Munich vs Koln

Marking their return from November’s international break on Friday night, Bayern Munich will welcome Koln to the Allianz.

With the rest of Europe’s elite domestic leagues making their respective returns this weekend, there are plenty of eye-catching betting promotions available.

Ahead of Friday’s Bundesliga battle, you can find all of the key Bayern Munich vs Koln H2H stats here.

Starting with the hosts, welcoming back Vincent Kompany to the touchline this weekend, Bayern Munich will be excited to make a return from November’s fortnight interval. Last seen heading into the final international break of 2026 with a 2-1 victory away at Mainz, it is no secret that the German giants are universally regarded as the standout contender to once again defend their Bundesliga crown this season. Marking their return sat at the top of the table, Bayern will be looking to make another public statement here. Getting their Champions League adventure underway with a real flurry and yet to suffer a single competitive defeat across all competitions so far this season, Kompany’s superstar squad have also gained a fearsome reputation for their free-scoring performances in the final third. In fact, the former Burnley boss has seen his squad notch 29 goals in their first nine Bundesliga appearances.

Along with welcoming Kompany back to the Allianz dugout this weekend, German international Jamal Musiala is also expected to make a first Bundesliga appearance since the middle of September. However, suffering from a muscle injury prior to November’s international break, former Liverpool star Luis Diaz remains on the sidelines.

Crowned as the new Ballon d’Or winner during an emotional ceremony in London last month, talismanic number nine Harry Kane will lead the line in Munich. Registering nine direct goal contributions in as many Bundesliga appearances this season (six goals, three assists), Michael Olise will partner Kane in the final third.

As for the visitors, while Koln might have eventually maintained their Bundesliga status last season, the Billy Goats appear destined for another relegation scrap this time around. Marking their respective return from November’s international break holding just a two-point buffer over the drop zone, Rene Wagner’s side couldn’t have asked for a tougher examination when they travel to Munich this weekend. Last seen heading into the fortnight interval with a 2-1 defeat at home against Bayer Leverkusen, Koln have mustered just a sole win from any of their previous eight Bundesliga appearances. Along with failing to find any kind of clinical edge in the final third, Friday’s guests will be concerned by a nightmare record against Bayern. Including a 5-1 drumming when they last travelled to the Allianz back on May 16th, they have lost each of their last six straight battles by an aggregate score of 19-4.

Yet to make a maiden Bundesliga appearance this season, German midfielder Timo Hubers remains on the sidelines with a serious knee injury. However, Wagner’s side could welcome back one-time Sparta Rotterdam youngster Ragnar Ache for the first time since the start of October.

While Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore might still be waiting to open his Bundesliga account, the England U21 international will feature in Munich. Bagging what turned out to be a consolation strike against Bayer Leverkusen last time out and featuring for Germany over the past fortnight, 20-year-old Said El Mala will lead the line on Friday night.

Excited to welcome Kompany back to the Allianz dugout on Friday night, Bayern Munich will be confident of laying down another domestic marker. Marking their return from November’s fortnight interval once again leading the chase at the top of the Bundesliga standings, the reigning German champions have yet to suffer a single defeat across any competition since opening the new campaign. Cruising their way to a routine 5-1 victory when they last welcomed Koln to the Allianz back in May, Bayern hold a dominant record against Friday’s guests. Winning their previous six consecutive Bundesliga battles by an aggregate score of 14-4, a free-scoring Bayern will be confident of putting on a show.

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Dowman, 16, started off the right flank for the Young Lions, and he scored the third goal for the home side on a wet Monday evening.

Divin Mubama, the Southampton striker, led the line while young Gunner Tommy Setford, who is spending the campaign on loan at Stevenage in League One, was between the sticks.

Dowman produced a stellar showing, capping off a well-crafted England goal as Harrison Armstrong seized upon a late mistake in the French backline, before squaring to the young forward to slot home into an unguarded net.

It follows on from his impressive display in the 1-0 defeat by Portugal last time out, where he was introduced for Amario Cozier-Duberry on the hour by Carsley.

While he could not find that elusive equaliser, he was bright in his substitute cameo on Friday.

It remains to be seen what role he could play in Arsenal’s trip to Newcastle United this weekend, before they host Borussia Dortmund and Manchester City at the Emirates Stadium next week.

#1804. When is Nations League draw? Start time, confirmed pot numbers and TV channel for quarter-finals

The 2026-27 Nations League draw for the quarter-finals takes place this week, as the business end of the competition comes into focus.

England are among the five teams to have qualified for the knockout phase, as things currently stand, with Thomas Tuchel’s side enjoying a near perfect group phase.

Their only defeat came against reigning world champions Spain on matchday one in September, though the Three Lions exacted revenge on Sunday night as they held on after being reduced to 10-men to seal a famous victory.

As a result, England topped Group A3 at Spain’s expense due to a superior goal difference and that means they are likely to avoid another European heavyweight in the quarter-finals.

Elsewhere, France sealed top spot in Group A1 with a 2-1 win over Turkey, while Belgium thumped Italy 4-1 to finish as runners-up.

In A2, Germany topped the table with a 5-0 thrashing of the Netherlands, who slipped to second on goal difference after such a swing.

Portugal’s position in Group A4 is still to be confirmed after they were humbled at home by Denmark in their first game since Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football.

The Nations League draw for the 2026/27 quarter-finals will take place on Friday, November 20, following the conclusion of the group phase fixtures.

As well as the quarter-final draw, the promotion/relegation play-offs draw will also be conducted.

Coverage of the draw is due to start at 11am GMT, with the draw itself expected to begin shortly afterwards.

The Nations League draw will take place in Nyon, Switzerland.

TV channel: In the UK, the draw will be televised live UEFA TV.

Live stream: You can also stream the draw for free online via the UEFA YouTube page.

Live blog: You can follow the draw as it happens on the day through Standard Sport’s live blog.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

The four group winners will be seeded in Pot 1, with the four runners-up will be unseeded in Pot 2.

*Portugal are guaranteed a Nations League quarter-final spot, though can still finish first or second in Group A4.

The Nations League quarter-finals, as well as the League A/B and League B/C promotion/relegation play-offs, will be played in March 2027.

#1803. Jurgen Klopp gushing in praise for Arsenal star: ‘He is a complete package’

Jurgen Klopp has talked up Arsenal’s Kai Havertz as ‘a complete package as a top player’ as he hopes the forward can have a big impact for Germany.

The 27-year-old has won 64 caps for his country, scoring 25 goals, and was in action as Germany beat Serbia 3-1 on Friday.

The former Chelsea man will be in the team on Monday night for the crucial Nations League clash with Netherlands, as Klopp looks to take his side into the quarter-finals.

The Germany boss has looked to build confidence in Havertz by talking up the forward’s qualities, which he feels can match up to almost anyone in the game.

‘I have often faced teams defended by Kai, and I know very well in tactical preparations that facing Kai is not an easy task. He is a complete package as a top player,’ said Klopp.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘Mikel Arteta relies heavily on him because Kai is always reliable to put in an extraordinary performance thanks to his technical capacity and intelligence.’

He added: ‘Kai and I have agreed that there is still huge potential that we want to develop further together in the national team.’

Havertz has not been in good goal-scoring form of late, netting just once in his last 13 appearances for club and country.

That was a crucial goal in a 1-0 Arsenal win over Liverpool, but finding the back of the net has not come easily for the Gunners star.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

He will look to improve his recent record in Berlin on Monday night as Germany try and topple the group-leaders, although Klopp says the long-term project is more important than short-term success.

‘We want success right now, but the process we have set in motion takes precedence over everything else,’ he said.

‘We want to put in a top performance, then we will see how that measures up against the Netherlands.

‘We are really looking forward to this game. We wanted this opportunity, now we have got it and we want to make the most of it.

‘[Netherlands have] basically got the same squad that played at the World Cup, that is the difference between us. We are in a period of transition right now.’

#1801. Martin Zubimendi stance on Chelsea transfer as Arsenal set asking price

Martin Zubimendi is seriously considering leaving Arsenal for the first time and has refused to rule out a move to Chelsea, according to reports in Spain.

Zubimendi is yet to start a Premier League game for Arsenal this season, with the concerning lack of game-time sparking speculation over his future at the Emirates Stadium.

The Spanish midfielder enjoyed a bright start to his Gunners career following a £60m move from Real Sociedad, earning rave reviews from Mikel Arteta this time last year.

But Zubimendi had lost his place in the Arsenal team by the end of the season, with a teenage Myles Lewis-Skelly instead starting the Champions League final against PSG.

The 27-year-old has continued to struggle for minutes this season and is now, for the first time, considering his future at the club.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Spanish outlet AS say Zubimendi has his eye on a January exit and is ‘open to everything’ following reports linking him with Chelsea, Real Madrid and Atletico Madrid.

Xabi Alonso is keen to strengthen his midfield options and knows Zubimendi well from his previous spell at Real Sociedad.

Zubimendi is contracted to Arsenal until 2030 but reports in Spain say the north London club will consider offers for the World Cup winner of at least £60m.

Last week, Zubimendi was forced to address speculation linking him with a move away from Arsenal while on international duty with Spain.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘To be honest, I’m sometimes surprised by the press too,’ he told Marca. ‘I understand that the winter transfer window is approaching and rumours can surface, but I think we need to be a bit more careful with what we publish.

‘Ultimately, everyone has a team they play for, and we need to respect that. I’ve also read that I might be close, but not at all.

‘Often a news story comes out and it seems that if it doesn’t come true, it’s quickly forgotten and nothing happens.

‘I’m learning how this world works and getting used to it, but sometimes I could avoid a lot of the messages I receive because of this kind of news.’

Zubimendi also revealed he was warned about a possible lack of minutes by Arteta ahead of the 2026/27 campaign.

Arteta bolstered his midfield options over the summer, with Arsenal spending £75m to sign Brazil international Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United.

‘I spoke with Mikel at the beginning of the season,’ Zubimendi added. ‘As he does with all the players, he explained the plan to me.

‘He warned me that there were new signings and that there would be playing time for everyone. And here we are, fighting for it.

‘I understand because, for me, we’re among the five best teams in Europe. There are some fantastic players. New signings have arrived in my position, and there were already some very good players.

‘I’m also part of that competition that makes it so difficult to get playing time. I’m calm and happy with how I’m handling this situation.

‘It’s something I’ve never experienced before, and I think you learn from these situations too. Besides, it’s in moments like these that you need the people around you the most, and they’re there for you.

‘I’m patient. When you’ve been playing a lot of minutes and your role changes to not playing as much, I’m able to see the positive side.

‘I think everything passes, that just like last year the opposite happened to me and I played practically everything, this can change very quickly.’

#1800. Arsenal: Declan Rice agrees new long-term contract as Gunners target period of dominance

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Declan Rice has agreed a new long-term contract with Arsenal.

The midfielder began talks with the club over improved terms earlier in the year and those have accelerated in recent weeks.

It is understood that a verbal agreement has now been reached and Rice will soon put pen to paper on the deal.

The long-term extension will see Rice receive a huge pay rise, taking him up to bracket of Bukayo Saka as the club’s best-paid player on around £350,000-a-week.

Rice has established himself as a central figure in Mikel Arteta’s side ever since he arrived for £105million from West Ham in 2023.

The 27-year-old secured his first piece of silverware for the Gunners last season, winning the Premier League in a campaign in which he played 69 matches for club and country.

Rice’s previous deal was set to expire in 2028 but both parties have been relaxed about the situation, even after he entered the final two years of that contract.

The England international made it clear that he wanted to stay at Arsenal, while the club never had any intention of losing him.

Rice follows Arteta in committing his future to the club. Bukayo Saka, William Saliba and Gabriel are among those to have also signed new long-term contracts.

Arsenal are keen to tie down the core of their first-team squad as they target a period of dominance over the next few years.

Discussions have been ongoing with Jurrien Timber, who like Rice would have been out of contract in 2028.

Those talks are also believed to be nearing a conclusion after an agreement was improved on an improved contract for the Dutchman.

#1799. Pochettino would tell Guardiola to take USA job

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Mauricio Pochettino would tell Pep Guardiola to take the job as the United States head coach if he is offered the chance.

Despite signing a new four-year contract with the USA after leading them to the World Cup quarter-finals in July, Pochettino last week agreed to take over at Manchester United following the dismissal of Michael Carrick.

Guardiola is reportedly US Soccer's favoured candidate to replace Pochettino having left Manchester City at the end of last season.

Asked what he would tell Guardiola if the USA made an official approach, Pochettino replied: "Take it.

"Why? Because it’s a perfect moment to arrive at the federation. Everything is on the right path, in the right direction. Of course, take it.

"Of course, you are going to find really good players, good people – the players can fit his style."

Six goals on Saturday to set ourselves on the front foot. ROLL THE HIGHLIGHTS! https://t.co/J6y6JrEuzv

— U.S. Soccer Men's National Team (@USMNT) November 15, 2026

Pochettino was seen as a coup for USA when he took over and he now believes the role has evolved into one of the most desirable jobs in football.

"The vision from Europe, I promise it is completely different after the World Cup," said Pochettino.

"Now, being head coach of the USA is more prestigious.

"If Manchester United or Real Madrid or Barcelona is coming for the US coach, you start to think about that.

"If you are another coach – maybe [Antonio] Conte, someone else, you say ‘Oh, this is a great opportunity.’ [In my case], ‘Oh, Pochettino, from Chelsea he goes to the US and now to Manchester United.’

"I think that is, for me, the beginning of the change for the future: that idea that the American player can be very good, can be very competitive.

"The talent is here; it’s so powerful in this country. I think that is why I feel proud. Maybe that was our job, because I don’t believe in coincidence. That has happened because something needed to happen.

"Now the tough job is done. Maybe now [the United job] is my reward because of this tough job."

Pochettino will hope to help United out of the relegation zone in his first match at the helm away against Liverpool on Sunday.

#1797. Who will England face in Nations League quarter-final? Next opponents confirmed after Spain win

England are on course to record their best ever performance in the Nations League, having qualified for the quarter-finals as group winners ahead of world champions Spain.

Including its inaugural season in 2018/19, the Three Lions have competed in every single Nations League campaign, experiencing some highs and the lowest of lows.

From topping their group and qualifying for the Nations League finals and finishing third to suffering a shock relegation in 2022/23 and then immediate promotion, England have done almost everything except win the competition.

Having started the 2026/27 campaign with a loss to Spain, despite leading 2-1 at one stage, England bounced back in style by beating the Czechs twice and then thumping Croatia 7-0 in a remarkable, record-breaking rout.

Another win over Croatia followed at Wembley to confirm a top-two finish in the group and qualify for the Nations League knockout stage.

England then beat Spain in a one-game shootout in Madrid to win the group and with that, potentially securing, an easier quarter-final tie next March.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

As a result of finishing top in Group A3, England’s confirmed potential Nations League quarter-final opponent are Belgium and the Netherlands after they were pipped to top spot in Group A1 and A2 by France and Germany respectively.

England’s remaining possible quarter-final opponents will be revealed on Tuesday night, but as things currently stand, they could be drawn against either Portugal, Denmark or Norway.

The draw for the 2026/27 Nations League quarter-final will take place on Friday, November 20 with the ties scheduled to take place in March 2027.

#1796. Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman smashes Jude Bellingham England Under-21 record

Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman has broken two England Under-21 records previously held by Jude Bellingham in a matter of days.

The 16-year-old became the youngest player ever to play for the Three Lions at Under-21 level when he came off the bench on Friday in a 1-0 defeat to Portugal.

Dowman then started against France at Aston Gate on Monday night, scoring a dramatic late winner in a 3-2 victory.

His appearance against Portugal broke Bellingham’s record as youngest England Under-21 player and his goal against France broke the Real Madrid superstar’s record as youngest to score at this level.

Dowman was 16 years and 320 days when he scored in Bristol on Monday, while Bellingham was 17 years and 67 days old when he made his debut against Kosovo in 2020, scoring on his first appearance for England Under-21s.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Also on the scoresheet for England in the friendly win over France were Tottenham’s Mikey Moore and Manchester City’s Divin Mubama, who is on loan at Southampton this season.

Manchester City’s Rico Lewis captained Lee Carsley’s side, while the likes of Brighton’s Jack Hinshelwood and Liverpool’s Trey Nyoni were also in the starting XI.

It was Dowman who was making yet more history, though, having already become the youngest player to score in the Premier League and to make an appearance in the Champions League.

When Arsenal won the title last season, he also became the youngest player to lift the Premier League trophy.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The incredible talent does not turn 17 until December 31 and will hope to get more run outs for Arsenal before then, although he has only had one very brief substitute appearance for the Gunners since his red card against Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup on October 27.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta was clearly fuming with Dowman when he was shown a straight red card for reacting to a heavy challenge against Fleetwood, giving the youngster stern words as he left the field.

Arteta said: ‘I haven’t seen the reaction to my reaction, whether it is positive or negative. But you need to understand the context and the relationship that I have with him and what we discussed just before we went out.

‘But, I don’t know. You can have another reaction. If you see the reaction of my father and my mother with me some days you might say “I don’t like the reaction”. For me, it was the best reaction to be who I am.’

He added: ‘The reaction when I don’t win, you want to know what my reaction is? I am [angry] big time.

‘So, we need to be ready for that. This is the environment and this is the reality, otherwise we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland, we are in the Premier League and this level.

‘We look after him so much that you cannot imagine. But at the same time we are going to demand from him, like everybody else, because he needs to earn the right to play. Because the other boys, what are they going to tell me? You need to be fair.’

#1795. Moreira discusses first Belgium goal, ‘special’ Milan group and learning in Italy: “I’ll always remember”

Last night, Diego Moreira scored his first goal for Belgium and AC Milan will be very happy to see their investment continuing to shine.

It’s fair to say that Moreira has been a revelation for Milan. His arrival came out of nowhere, with a deal first reported by FootballKush and then it was picked up by the biggest sources in football. His first appearance was a struggle against Juventus, but the rest, as they say, is history.

Goals have come regularly, with huge appearances that have defined the Rossoneri’s season already. For example, the goal against Inter, with two assists to accompany it. He’s perhaps been the signing of the season in Italy and there’d maybe be a conversation about Europe, too.

After scoring against Italy, Moreira spoke to Sky, looking at the team’s performance, playing with Kevin De Bruyne and the feeling of grabbing his first goal for his country, as MilanNews relays.

“I’m very happy with my first goal for the national team. It was a special moment because my family was there. It’s a day I’ll always remember.”

Mancini said that you deserved to win and that you are a very strong team…

“We have some very strong players up front, like Doku, De Bruyne, but I think that in the end it’s a sport where everyone is needed and we all played a great game.”

What does it mean to play with a player like De Bruyne?

“De Bruyne is special; it’s a pleasure to have him with us because he sees things that others don’t see, he has a lot of experience and we’re happy to have him in our team.”

What do you take from this experience with the national team at AC Milan?

“I learned a lot in Italy because it’s a league with a lot of experienced players. Playing for the national team and for AC Milan are two very positive things, and I’m very happy.”

How do you recover in Europe after a difficult start?

“It’s difficult but we’re working towards this. We have to be prepared and we have players who will help us with this.”

Then, in the mixed zone, he was also intercepted by MilanNews, where he also answered a few questions about the Rossoneri.

Diego, you scored in your first Milan derby, just like Kaká, Shevchenko, and Ronaldinho before you. How have you settled in at AC Milan?

“I’m very happy. At AC Milan, I’m surrounded by a special group, with many great players. Having them around me helps me a lot, especially in terms of experience. It’s true, the match against Inter was special. I’ll continue to work hard and give my best.”

Good in Serie A, bad in the Europa League: why this two-faced Milan?

“I’m on the national team right now, and you’re asking me about Milan?”

Belgium practically overwhelmed Italy, your current footballing nation. It ended 4-1, but the scoreline could have been eight or nine goals…

“It’s something special, and we’re very happy. It was an important match, so winning and scoring was really nice.”

#1794. Mauricio Pochettino reveals Manchester United U-turn after Pep Guardiola talks

Mauricio Pochettino says he has a point to prove at Manchester United, after revealing his conversation with Pep Guardiola prior to sealing a return to club management.

The Argentine was appointed new Man United head coach last week, succeeding Michael Carrick who was sacked as a result of a disappointing start to the season with the side languishing in the Premier League relegation zone.

This will be the 54-year-old’s first job in club management since leaving Chelsea at the end of the 2023-24 season and fourth overall in England’s top-flight following spells at Southampton and Tottenham.

Despite the announcement, Pochettino does not officially start work at Man Utd until Wednesday as he has been granted permission to finish up with the United States Men’s National Team [USMNT] before reporting to Carrington.

6-0 up from the first-leg of the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti, it is expected to be a routine exercise for USA in the early hours of Wednesday morning [UK time] for what is Pochettino’s farewell game.

Speaking with the Telegraph in preparation of saying goodbye to international management, Pochettino said he admitted to Guardiola in September that he missed the day-to-day element of club management.

“I am ready [to return],” he said. “This is what I miss a little bit. I miss to be, every day, with something here.

“Guardiola asked me when I was at the game, he said, ‘Oh, you don’t want to come back to the Premier League?’ I said, ‘No, I’m happy here.’

“[He said] ‘Yeah, but you don’t miss, every day, to…’ I say, ‘A little bit, yes, because you think now today, and then we have December camp against Jamaica for the MLS [players in the pool].

“But after, you need to wait [until] March. What do you do? You need to watch games, you need to travel – administrative things. That is nice, it’s good.

“But every day, to be involved: press conference, training, everything … this type of possibility, like with United, you say yes. I want that. I want to prove myself again.”

By Saikat Mandal | 16 Nov 2026 16:37

Liverpool are reportedly showing a keen interest in signing Brazilian youngster Arthur Dias.

Liverpool have also been linked with a move for former defender Jarell Quansah, although it would likely take a substantial offer to bring him back to Anfield.

There is little harm in building a pool of exciting young defenders at the club, but whether Liverpool would be prepared to pay £25m for Dias remains to be seen.
