#1717. Building in Barca and the Jim Reaper strikes again

Greetings, Tim here on blog duty today and I am going right back to Arseblog’s roots by writing from Barcelona. I am here of course because Arsenal Women earned a very creditable (and slightly unexpected given how this season has gone for them) draw against the current Champions League holders Barcelona.

Of course, Renee Slegers’ side did beat Barca the last time the teams met in the 2025 Final and that was only slightly less of an upset than this result. As expected, Arsenal rose their luck a little with Barca putting up 24 shots and 2.4XG. But Arsenal have put up similar numbers in games this season roughly 176 times and not won so I am happy to be on the receiving end of a little serendipity.

Frida Maanum gave Arsenal a first half lead before her compatriot Caroline Graham Hansen equalised in the second half. You can read Renee Slegers’ post-match press conference here and my take on the match here if you are so inclined. Up next is a six pointer for Champions League qualification at home to London City Lionesses on Sunday which Arsenal just have to win. Obviously we will have all the usual coverage of that game for you.

I also had the pleasure of meeting fellow Arseblog / Arsenal Vision colleague Phil Costa for lunch and in Barcelona, for a seafood and beer lover, a long lunch in balmy 20 degree conditions was very welcome indeed!

Elsewhere, there were plenty of Arsenal players in action for their countries. Martin Zubimendi played the full 90 minutes for Spain in their 2-0 away win at Czechia. Usually I would wince at a sentence that featured ‘Arsenal player x’ and ‘full 90 minutes’ but I think Zubimendi could use those minutes for physical reasons and for psychological reasons as he tries to plot his way back into a very crowded Arsenal midfield.

Mikel Merino came on for the final 24 minutes of that game and David Raya kept his gloves clean on the bench. Declan Rice played 77 minutes of England’s 2-1 win over Croatia at Wembley in which Harry Kane scored his 417th goal for England, 461 of which have been penalties (citation needed). Eze was an unused sub and he’s another I wouldn’t have minded seeing get some minutes to build rhythm and confidence.

Riccardo Calafiori played the full 90 of Italy’s 3-1 win over France. Jurrien Timber and Kai Havertz could be in action tonight as Netherlands play Greece and Germany play away at Serbia. Fingers crossed for both. These are two players I would not mind seeing unused but I doubt that will be the case.

Meanwhile, the big news elsewhere was that Michael Carrick was finally officially sacked by Manchester United. He had still been taking training this week despite everyone knowing that he was for the chop. I hope he filled his coat pockets with as many of the milk and ketchup sachets as he could from the canteen.

He was clearly out of his depth and had been stalking the United dugout looking like a haunted Noel Gallagher for what feels like months. Steve Holland has also left and Ben White’s recent recall to the England team resurfaced old wounds as he was asked about his reasons for making himself unavailable for a while for his country. White refuses to be drawn on it.

I am biased, of course, but I know who I think has emerged better from this sorry saga and his surname is a colour not a country. Having taken in Spurs and Chelsea already, it looks like Mauricio Pochettino is about to go three for three on his tour of the Premier League’s most evil institutions. If hell really does exist, this man will regard an eternal stint of fire and brimstone as something of a vacation. Maybe working for the Jim Reaper at United is his penance for accepting work from Chelsea and Spurs.

For further reading, check out my weekly column in which I look at three ways in which Arsenal have evolved this season.

#1715. An Arseblog update

It’s around 10.30am on Friday, November 6th 2026. I’m in my hotel room in London, doing a few Arseblog bits on my laptop, and getting ready for the launch of the The 22 in the Big Red that night.

My phone rings. It’s a Dublin number but one not in my contacts. Typically I wouldn’t answer, but I think I know who it probably is. I’m right. It’s the Oncology department of the hospital I was admitted to a couple of weeks ago. They have news.

“Can you come into us on Monday afternoon at 2.30?”

“Great, we’ll see you then. Oh, and you should bring somebody with you. It’s a lot of information to take in.”

As of this moment, I’m still not 100% on all the details. I had another scan yesterday, and I have a procedure scheduled for Tuesday which will give us more information. However, they’ve already laid out a plan for three months of chemo, which is kind of why I’m writing this.

My very, very strong instinct with any medical stuff is to keep it private. And I suppose if I was a guy who had a regular 9 to 5 and went to the office every day, I could do that. However, the privilege of my work is that it is very public facing. I do the stuff, you read the stuff and listen to the stuff, and you are part of my life in a very big way; in the same way – even if it it’s just for a few minutes each morning, or a couple of hours in your headphones – that I’m part of yours.

Which isn’t say I feel like I owe anyone an explanation, but this is my reality now, and for what’s likely to be an arduous road ahead for a while. Unfortunately, that makes it part of your reality too. I will say, I’m not going to document my ‘journey’. Fair play to anyone who does. Whatever you need to do to get through the challenges an illness presents, it’s just not really who I am. I don’t even do video on podcasts about football, so I’m not gonna start now for something like this!

But I do need the distraction of work, of Arsenal, of football and all its ludicrousness and drama, and this incredible community that has grown over the near 25 years of Arseblog’s existence. I’ve missed it this week, despite the fact it’s been such a difficult time in this household. We’ve gone through all the normal human reactions and emotions, and the whole thing was compounded by the fact I came back from London with the single worst stomach bug I’ve ever had in my life. To be honest, that felt a bit mean from the universe. Here, have a bit of this, and just to make you feel worse, you will require about twenty visits to the bathroom every day. It’s a bit like one of those days where every set of traffic lights you hit turns red as you approach, but the traffic lights also make your arse hurt. Fuck off!

So, I’m going to be around, and I’m gonna do my best to do what I normally do. I need as much normal as I can get, because right now too much isn’t. But there will be days when I’m not, or I can’t be, and I’m happy to let the lads pick up the slack as much as possible. To preempt many messages and thoughts, I know what the priority is, and I’m not going to push myself at the expense of my health or getting better. I have a vested interest in, you know, making a full recovery. I’m not going to risk doing anything that might conflict with that.

But I also feel like the best way to navigate this is to not let it take over my life, or to define who I am. I’m still just an Irish bloke with a website about Arsenal first and foremost, and the last week or so has made me feel strangely protective of that. A dose of perspective is a really interesting thing, I know what the most important thing is right now, but that can only succeed if I remain myself. I hope that makes sense.

Some lads kicking a ball around a football pitch is, in the grand scheme of things, not that important. But hasn’t that always been the case? Football is so intrinsic to all of us, and we give so much of our time and energy to it, because we (well most of us) understand the absurdity of giving so much of ourselves to something that is completely out of our control. We can pretend otherwise, but that’s all part of the fun too. Lucky socks and lucky shirts and matchday routines. Our brain’s way of trying to make it feel like we have some influence, because we need that sliver of pretence, but in the end it’s about whether some millionaire at the back post can apply the finish.

I suppose at least this shit waited until there was an Interlull. Thanks for that.

I’m lucky because I have an amazing wife and daughter, and family and friends, who will be with me every step of the way. Their support thus far has been incredible, and I know I can count on it 100%. I’m going to listen to the doctors and the medical team and do whatever it is they ask of me. They seem to know what they’re on about, which is reassuring. Almost like they’re experts or something. We should listen to them.

I know as well that wider support from the Arseblog community will be forthcoming, and I just wanted to say in advance that I appreciate it hugely. I suspect that replying to every message is going to be beyond me, and in normal circumstances that would bother me greatly. I always try to respond to every email I get, even if it takes me a while, but in this instance I hope you’ll understand if I don’t or can’t.

So that’s where we are. I still don’t know where we’ll end up or how we’ll get there, but despite the fact I’m scared and worried, I’m also positive and determined. I could really do without this, to be quite honest, but it is what it is, and the only way through is forward. I’ll keep you in the loop as much as I feel I can, and in the meantime if Arsenal could make my day to day life as stress free as possible, I’d really appreciate that.

Someone have a word with Mikel and the lads.

Strasbourg have reportedly made an approach for Swansea City head coach Vitor Matos.

The Welsh club have been one of the surprise packages of the EFL, with the Swans currently sitting in sixth position in the Championship table.

However, despite penning a long-term contract at Swansea, it appears that the 38-year-old is prepared to leave for pastures new.

Instead, Strasbourg have accumulated just 10 points from as many matches to sit in 13th position in the Ligue 1 table.

Matos is said to be keen to take any opportunity that arises at Stade de la Meinau, putting his job at Swansea in doubt.

With Strasbourg facing Brest, Le Havre, Lorient and Angers in their next four contests, Oliveira could be given at least some of that period to turn things around.

#1713. Report: Decision made, Liverpool ready to agree £55m deal today

Liverpool are ready to strike a major deal today. Unfortunately, they'll be forced to wait to complete this one.

Liverpool spent an enormous amount of money over the last few years, with sporting director Richard Hughes moving the club away from "smart" signings and towards "big" signings. It's a strategy that hasn't worked out.

We know that because despite spending half a billion pounds, this isn't a team that particularly works. Liverpool need more signings if they're to move forward and need them in virtually every area of the pitch.

That will naturally cost a lot more money. Hopefully, the Reds are a bit smarter about this and look for a different kind of signing than the €100m+ deals which have proved problematic thus far.

One such deal is already on the cards, in fact, and reports indicate that Liverpool are ready to strike it now. Though, they'll be made to wait.

One of the most interesting deals Liverpool did strike under Hughes was for Ronald Araujo. Liverpool haven’t been one for massive loan deals in the past but they agreed one here.

Araujo joined for the season from Barcelona and has started life at Anfield wonderfully. He’s starting at right-back for now but is a natural centre-back, offering proper versatility and options in the back line.

Above all, though, he’s just playing well. It opens the door to buying him permanently, with a buy clause in his deal for a proper transfer. Liverpool just need to offer around €55m.

Marca reports that they’re ready to do just that. Araujo has impressed so much that as things stand, Liverpool want to trigger the clause and sign the Uruayan permanently.

All that’s really holding things back is the fact that the clause can’t be triggered until the end of the season. Though, that’s probably a good thing - Liverpool shouldn’t really rush here as there’s no real need. Get a full season out of Araujo and then assess the situation.

But things are heading in one direction, it seems. And that would mean many more years of Araujo.

#1711. It’ll be Ben White on the night

Arsenal lads were in action, and on the scoresheet, last night as England beat Spain 3-2 in Madrid. Ezri Konsa made it 2-0 with a close range header, Spain might wonder who was marking him (I think it was supposed to be Marc Cucurella) but the movement was really sharp. Then a couple of minute later, Ben White fired England into a 3-0 lead, with Cucurella also in close attendance.

Obviously I’m not especially invested in the national sides of other countries, but I was pleased for Ben White after all the nonsense he’s been through with England. The worst sections of the media have fanned the flames against him, and it doesn’t take much to rile up those who are already of a jingoistic persuasion. As we’ve seen since seen with stories about Steve Holland being hugely unpopular at Man Utd, there’s a common denominator, and it’s not Ben White.

Holland was the one who sparked the issue originally when he was working with Gareth Southgate, so hopefully another goal for the Arsenal defender (he got one a few months back I think), and being part of a famous win in Spain will win around some of those fans who were giving him stick. I also feel quite confident that even if there is a cohort who won’t forgive Ben White for the crime of Steve Holland being a dickhead, he probably won’t care too much. Look at the reactions of his teammates and manager to the goal, and that’s tells you plenty.

He was also involved in a minor scuffle going off at half-time, which also seemed to involved Konsa and Martin Zubimendi, but I’m sure it was just heat of the moment stuff. Although Spain got two back after England went down to 10 men, they made the fatal mistake of starting Mikel Merino. How was he supposed to come off the bench and get a vital goal then? Silly Luis de la Fuenta, bloke’s a fraud.

Elsewhere over the weekend, Viktor Gyokeres scored twice for Sweden, both from the penalty spot. We just need more penalties. This is the key to unlocking him. Riccardo Calafiori played the full 90 as Italy went down 4-1 to Belgium (ouch), Martin Odegaard played 90 as Norway beat Wales, and there are some more games to come this week with Germany facing Netherlands tonight (Kai v Timber), the Brazilians are in action in Singapore, and apparently Christos Tzolis is fit to play for Greece after having an MRI.

Maybe it’s my own recent experiences, but I don’t care for the idea he needs an MRI. I get it, it’s probably for his knee or hamstring or something, but it feels like if you need one of those to know if you’re fit, you’re probably not feeling 100% anyway. I guess this will be one Mikel Arteta will keep a close eye on tonight when Greece host Serbia and Tzolis inevitably starts. Ideally, these will be useful minutes for him, and help him deliver for us but you can’t help but worry considering he picked up an injury in the last Interlull.

Finally for today, it looks as if a Declan Rice contract extension is close. Speaking while on England duty, he said:

“A new contract is hopefully on the horizon soon. I’m extremely lucky to be at a club like Arsenal where the manager shows me so much trust and teammates who put so much energy and effort into to me.

“I’m extremely lucky not to have to worry about that stuff, and it makes playing football far more easier.”

This is, by any measure, a no-brainer. I don’t think there’s a club in the world that would turn him down if he were available, and his importance to Arsenal is just obvious. In a world when £100m+ transfers often struggle to provide value, this is one of the exceptions. If you went back to 2023 and had to do it all again, even if you added another £20m or £30m to the fee we paid West Ham, it would be worth it. It’s likely to be the kind of deal that sees him play out the rest of his prime years in red and white, and let’s hope there are more trophies along the way to accompany that.

Right, I have to leave it there for this morning. We will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on though. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

The pod should be out around around midday. Until then, have a good one – after which I’m gonna be off for a couple of days but the lads will keep things ticking here until I get back.

#1709. Chelsea and Manchester United lead race for Barcelona Fermin Lopez

By Alexis Pereira | 16 Nov 2026 23:37

Barcelona have reportedly received offers of up to £85m from the Premier League for Fermin Lopez, but the Spain midfielder wants to stay at Camp Nou and the club are preparing to discuss a new contract with his representatives. According to Sport, Chelsea and Manchester United are the two clubs most determined to sign the 23-year-old.

Long regarded as a promising player capable of bringing energy and drive off the bench, the attacking midfielder has gradually established himself as an important part of boss Hansi Flick’s system. His performances in recent months, particularly his two goals against Atletico Madrid, have strengthened his status further. At 23, he already has eight goals and seven assists in 15 appearances in all competitions this season.

His ability to get into the box, attack space from the second line and make a difference in the final 30 metres makes him a particularly valuable weapon for Barcelona. Lopez also brings strong intensity to the press and a verticality that complements the more organising midfielders in the Catalan squad. Unsurprisingly, the progress has not gone unnoticed in the transfer market, and several English clubs appear ready to invest heavily to persuade him to move.

According to Sport, Barcelona have received proposals from the Premier League for the attacking midfielder. Some reach £85m, a considerable amount that reflects the growing value of the Spain international, who has 12 caps. Chelsea and Manchester United are the two sides most determined to sign him, while the identity of the other two suitors has not been revealed.

Chelsea’s interest is not new. The London club tried in the last summer window with a proposal estimated at £59.5m, which did not even lead to real discussions with the Catalan hierarchy. This time the figures mentioned are much higher and leave Barcelona with an important decision to make.

From a sporting point of view, losing such a decisive and versatile player would be difficult to replace. Financially, however, a £85m fee could give interesting room for manoeuvre to a board that remains mindful of its economic constraints. It remains to be seen whether the club are genuinely willing to listen to such offers.

Barcelona’s main argument for keeping him may also be the most important: Lopez does not want to leave. He is strongly attached to the club, where he wants to keep progressing and put down roots, and he is not particularly tempted by approaches from the Premier League. The number seven has even said he wishes to end his career in Catalonia.

That position makes the sporting department’s job easier. According to Sport, Barcelona plan to meet his representatives soon to discuss a new contract improvement, with the aim of raising his salary to reflect his new status in Flick’s squad.

Lopez already extended his contract until 2031 in January 2026 and has a release clause of £425m. The Catalan club intend to keep protecting one of their most valuable assets, and in the face of the English millions, Barcelona seem to be considering a reward for their rising star rather than a departure.

#1708. Opinion: Liverpool have done it, Mo Salah regen is coming to Reds' first-team

Mo Salah's regen is coming to Liverpool's first-team. The Reds have already found him.

For much of last summer, the conversation focused on Richard Hughes' plans to replace the club legend. Liverpool knew Salah was leaving after agreeing to cancel the final year of his contract in January.

There was a plan in place. The club already had the perfect replacement lined-up. Yan Diomande had talked up his father's love for Liverpool.

The Ivorian was putting in some breathtaking performances at RB Leipzig, a club from where Liverpool have brought in a fair few players over the last half a decade.

And yet - the move didn't happen. Diomande opted to reject the Reds. He wanted the allure of Paris and later Madrid.

How Liverpool planned to replace Mo SalahAmid Diomande's rejection, there was a final frantic scramble towards the end of the summer window. Liverpool made offers for Ismaila Sarr and Yankuba Minteh. But both of those offers were rejected. Their respective clubs demanded so much money that it was simply unfeasible for the Reds to pay it. So the solution the Reds concocted to replace Salah was to rotate their attackers. They signed two left-wingers in Victor Munoz, Bradley Barcola to add to their existing duo of Cody Gakpo and Rio Ngumoha. Now the four of them are rotating every game, with Ngumoh and Munoz playing on the right the most often so far. It's definitely a temporary solution. Especially because Liverpool might soon have a long-term player joining Iraola's first-team squad.

#1707. Man United Confidential: Jim Ratcliffe makes new 'brutal' cutbacks to ex-players' charity, Nathan Collins and Calvin Bassey among January targets, Luke Shaw eyes Anfield return and why club confiscated two anti-owner banners

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 12:15 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 03:42 EST, 11 November 2026

Sir Jim Ratcliffe is known for being ruthless – as Michael Carrick may be about to find out – and it appears as though the Association of Former Manchester United Players has once again paid the price.

Two years ago, Ratcliffe made front-page news at Christmas after it emerged he was cutting a yearly £40,000 donation to the AFMUP charity, which has been helping ex-United players since 1985.

Last week organisers were informed at the last minute that the second of its two annual dinners couldn’t be staged as usual in the Manchester Suite at Old Trafford and would have to move elsewhere.

So while plans were being made for Sir Alex Ferguson’s glittering 40th anniversary bash in the Heritage Suite on Friday night, the AFMUP had to rely on Hotel Football – part-owned by Gary Neville and the Class of ’92 – coming to the rescue to host their event over the road 24 hours earlier. Ferguson, it has to be said, has been a big supporter of the charity over the years.

There are now concerns that AFMUP will never be allowed back to Old Trafford with United understood to be insisting on a total of 400 guests, which is double what the charity can provide.

Previously, the AFMUP gave half of the £40,000 donation back to the club to hire the suite in April and September, raising additional funds through ticket sales and auctions.

Sir Jim Ratcliffe (left) is known for being ruthless and it appears as though the Association of Former Manchester United Players has once again paid the price

When Neville challenged Ratcliffe over the ‘cruel decision’ to cut the donation in a one-on-one interview in March last year and said the club should consider organising the dinner itself and asking current players to attend, the minority owner replied: ‘Well nobody suggested that, I would have supported that.’

As a result, United chief executive Omar Berrada joined Ferguson and former CEO David Gill at the dinner the following month – when Neville, Andy Cole and Jonny Evans were also present – and donated a VIP package for the auction worth £20,000.

Director of football Jason Wilcox then appeared at the next event in September and gave a rare interview on stage. In April of this year, Bryan Robson and Steve Bruce formed a popular double act as the main attraction.

Thursday’s dinner, which had already been moved from September 24 due to a double booking, was a celebration of the life of Duncan Edwards, who would have been 90 on October 1. Former chairman Martin Edwards and Gill were both present along with former goalkeeper Alex Stepney.

The AFMUP’s official filmmaker and publicist John Gubba highlighted the latest setback on his Man Utd The Religion YouTube channel, saying: ‘While the red carpet is being rolled out for Fergie, the club have been brutally abandoning the former players’ association.

‘The latest cutbacks by Sir Jim Ratcliffe have resulted in another kick in the teeth for the AFMUP. Staging their big event at the Theatre of Dreams was always a status that made the former players and their guests feel part of the football club. Being turfed out at short notice leaves a bitter taste.’ You can watch the full video here.

United sources say the club helped to facilitate an alternative venue at Hotel Football due to unavailability in the stadium, and insist that the charity will be welcome back to Old Trafford in future.

Berrada was present at Ferguson’s celebration dinner on Friday in which the United chief executive spoke about the importance of building a culture at Old Trafford.

He was one of 100 invited guests for the event to mark 40 years since Ferguson was appointed as United manager, moving from Aberdeen to replace Ron Atkinson in November 1986.

A number of Ferguson’s old players were present and posed for pictures with him including Michael Carrick, Brian McClair, Edwin van der Sar, Robin van Persie, David May, Wes Brown, Paul Parker, Dion Dublin, Denis Irwin, Jesper Blomqvist, Ryan Giggs, Gary Pallister, Javier Hernandez, Clayton Blackmore, Jonny Evans, John O’Shea, Darren Fletcher, Ronny Johnsen, Lee Martin, Nemanja Vidic and Quinton Fortune.

Ferguson’s former No2 Mike Phelan was also there along with Gill and kit man Albert Morgan.

There were 100 invited guests for the event to mark 40 years since Sir Alex Ferguson (third right) was appointed as United manager in November 1986

Luke Shaw is targeting a return to action away at Liverpool a week on Sunday, Confidential understands.

The 31-year-old has not featured since October 10 when he played 90 minutes against Tottenham, missing seven games through to the current international break.

That absence badly exposed United's lack of depth at left back, an area the hierarchy failed to address in the transfer window despite a clear need. Diogo Dalot, who was targeted by fans when he came off against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday, has played poorly while filling in on his unfavoured side.

With Patrick Dorgu now back in the mix, too, Shaw is hoping to be in contention for the trip to Anfield in what would be a timely boost for a defence that has conceded the joint-most goals in all competitions of any team in Europe’s top five leagues this season.

Nothing has undermined Carrick's time as United head coach more than the defensive problems that have seen his team concede 15 goals in their last five games.

United chose to delay the overhaul of their defence until next year when they focused on rebuilding the midfield last summer, but it has proved to be a costly misjudgment with Matthijs de Ligt only just returning to action after a year out and a spate of injuries to Shaw, Lisandro Martinez, Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui.

It may force United into the transfer market in January and Confidential understands Brentford centre back Nathan Collins and Fulham’s Calvin Bassey have joined Jarrad Branthwaite of Everton on the list of potential targets.

United also want a striker after failing to offload Joshua Zirkzee and sign cover for Benjamin Sesko in the summer, but a loan deal is more likely.

Brentford's Nathan Collins and Fulham's Nigeria star Calvin Bassey have both joined United's list of centre-back targets

As if the prospect of relegation isn’t nightmarish enough for United after they dropped to 18th place in the table, the cost of going down would be astronomical.

Although parachute payments from the Premier League would cushion the fall in the unlikely event that United are relegated, kit sponsors adidas have the option to scrap their record £900million, 10-year deal which was announced in 2023 but only came into effect last year.

Under the terms of the contract, the German sportswear giant can cancel it if they give the club one year’s notice. Adidas can also halve their annual payment to £45m if United aren’t playing in the Premier League, and hit the club with a £10m annual penalty if they are not in the Champions League.

Two banners protesting against United’s owners were confiscated by stewards during Sunday’s 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

One that read ‘Jim Can’t Fix This’ was seized because its connection to Jimmy Savile was deemed to be inappropriate. Another declaring ‘We Don’t Want A New Stadium, We Want New Owners’ was taken down because it was blocking the view of some fans.

Club insiders say protests will always be allowed as long as they remain within the regulations. United kept a close eye on Sunday’s demonstration with a more visible police presence in the Stretford End and stewards asking fans as they entered that section of the stadium which group they were with.

The protest, which once again involved green and gold balloons being released before kick-off, was jointly organised by The Red Army, The 1958, Manchester United Youth Supporters Club, South Stand United and Retro Reds.

However, it seemed like a strange decision to confiscate the banners considering that United were in possession of them for more than 30 hours before kick-off since 10am on Saturday morning.

They are stored in the same place in the Stretford End before every game, so it was odd for United to demand that they be taken down when they could have refused for them to be handed out in the first place.

A banner protesting against United's owners was confiscated during the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa

While goalkeeper Senne Lammens was giving his worst performance in a United shirt against Villa on Sunday, the man he replaced at Old Trafford was faring a little better in Turkey.

Andre Onana kept a clean sheet in Trabzonspor’s win over Alanyaspor as they moved into second place in the Super Lig table behind Galatasaray.

It came three days after a Europa League defeat by Freiburg when Onana couldn’t resist a little light ribbing of English reporters at the game.

Asked by journalists from Daily Mail Sport and the BBC for a quick word, the Cameroon international didn’t disappoint. ‘I don’t speak English, bro,’ Onana said, in perfect English. Classic.

#1705. Divine Dowman does it again

It’s Andrew A covering for Andrew M, who’s playing hooky again. I suppose after 24 years of writing this blog, a few bad habits are bound to creep in…

I’m not going to lie, it’s been a difficult week. Fortunately, a lifetime of watching Arsenal has given me plenty of practice at making bad jokes when I don’t know what else to say.

It’s either that or tears, and my eye juice reserves are running low after reading just a fraction of the thousands of messages you sent over the weekend. Bluesky, Reddit, X, Discord, Facebook, Patreon. Wherever I looked, there you were, sending love to Blogs. It was beautiful to see.

And to the handful of you who got in touch with me or people I know because you thought Friday’s update was about my health, please hold that thought. I’m fine. Touch wood. There are, in fact, two Andrews at Arseblog, and I’m the other one.

Having been crowned the “World’s Youngest Boy” by James on yesterday’s Arsecast Extra, Max Dowman set yet another record last night, becoming England under-21s’ youngest scorer with the winner in a 3-2 victory over France in filthy conditions in Bristol.

I’d planned to watch from kick-off, but gave up when I realised the game wasn’t on any of the 5,000 channels I pay £150 a month for. Then I saw on social media that Ethan Nwaneri, playing as a number 10, had laid on a couple of goals. So I did the clever thing and googled it. Turns out I needed the official England app and an account. Eyes still rolling, I tried to set up a login, only to find out I already had one. Cue the password reset process, verification codes and me losing the will to live. Just let me watch some fucking children play football in the rain!

By the time I got the stream, it was nearly half-time. At least that gave me a chance to catch up on Nwaneri’s two assists, both of which were Ozil-esque. First he drove down the left and slipped a neat ball inside for Mikey Moore, currently on loan at Cologne, to finish. Then came a teasing dink to the back post that Southampton’s Divin Mubama met first time. Given how little Nwaneri has played for Dortmund lately, it was a welcome reminder of what he can do.

It feels a bit silly to say Max, who was named player of the match, looked comfortable at this level when he’s already got a Premier League winners’ medal next to his GCSE textbooks, but he really did.

Watching him is like reading someone’s really nice handwriting. Even the everyday stuff looks lovely. A touch to bring the ball under control, a little turn, and suddenly the defender who was right up his arse is looking at the back of his shirt. I’ll never get tired of watching him do that.

As both sides made changes, I expected Lee Carsley to take him off. Instead, he played the full 90 and dug Arsenal teammate Tommy Setford out of a hole. The goalkeeper was at fault for the only goal in Friday’s defeat to Portugal and had another difficult night, spilling a cross into his own net. The rain hardly helped, and the 20-year-old has been doing well on loan at Stevenage, but it was a horrible one to concede.

When Brest’s Giovani Versini whipped in an equaliser with five minutes left, it looked like England would have to settle for a draw, but Dowman’s tap-in settled it with a minute to spare. Who knows, Dowman and Nwaneri could be on the same pitch again next week when Dortmund visit the Emirates.

Elsewhere, Group 2 of League A of the UEFA Nations League (catchy naming scheme, lads) served up another bonkers evening. Jurrien Timber scored twice in the Netherlands’ 7-0 win over Christos Tzolis’ Greece on Friday, only for the Dutch to lose 5-0 to Kai Havertz’s Germany in Berlin. There were some lovely goals from the Germans – including two from Florian Wirtz – who are finding their feet under Jurgen Klopp. Timber and Havertz both came off midway through the second half, seemingly unscathed. Timber’s pride aside, anyway.

Tzolis, meanwhile, was cleared to play after an MRI scan and got through 88 minutes of Greece’s 1-0 win over Serbia. All three sides finished on 11 points, with Germany and the Netherlands going through on goal difference at Greece’s expense.

Tonight, Martin Odegaard’s Norway face Denmark, while Viktor Gyokeres will look to extend his record-breaking scoring run for Sweden away at Poland. Piero Hincapie’s Ecuador take on Bolivia, Big Gabi and Bruno are in Singapore with Brazil, and Cristhian Mosquera and Marli Salmon are in action for Spain under-21s and England under-19s, respectively.

Closer to home, The Athletic ran two Arsenal contract stories in quick succession. James reports that Timber has agreed a new long-term deal, while David Ornstein says Declan Rice’s extension will take him through to 2031. Arsenal already had the option to keep Rice until 2029, so the new deal effectively buys them two more years and gives him a sizeable pay rise for the next four and a half. If he keeps playing as he has been, I can’t imagine many Arsenal fans quibbling with that.

For what it’s worth, we’ve heard on the grapevine that David Raya’s new contract is all but done, too, which means the club are making good progress with the lads whose deals expire in 2028, a list that also includes Odegaard, Havertz, Mikel Merino and our two backup keepers.

There was an interesting discussion on Arsenal Vision’s ‘Friday Night Clive’ podcast about Arsenal elongating their “winning window” while having one eye on the next iteration of the team. If you hand expensive new contracts to players hurtling towards their thirties, you leave yourself financially exposed and potentially blocking pathways for up-and-coming talent. No doubt the club and manager are keenly aware of that. I just wonder how much you can expect the latter to focus on the faraway future when the dynasty he craves has to start in the here and now.

If this week has taught me anything, it’s that there’s something to be said for seizing the day. Admittedly, that’s easier when it’s Arsenal’s money I’m volunteering to spend.

If you’re about to part with some of your own (smooth segue, Allen) this year’s Arseblog Christmas Gift Guide is up.

I spent some of last week rounding up Arsenal bits and pieces I’d be happy to find under the tree. Mostly, I wanted to point you towards the independent makers, artists and writers producing stuff I like. In many cases, what I’ve picked is just a small sample of what they do, so have a nose around.

If you’ve got a recommendation of your own, pop the link in the form at the bottom and I’ll take a look.

Right, I’d better crack on with the day job. Lewis is on duty tomorrow and, all being well, Andrew M should be back here before the week is out.

TuttoMercatoWeb reports that Liverpool want AC Milan centre-back Koni De Winter. It’s apparently an open secret that they’re interested, though not alone in that.

#1702. Gremio vs Bahia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 16 Nov 2026 23:58, Last updated: 17 Nov 2026 05:14

Gremio will host Bahia at their Arena do Gremio home in Porto Alegre on Wednesday night, for a crucial showdown that will have ramifications for both the Brasileirao's relegation battle and race for Copa Libertadores qualification.

The Tricolor dos Pampas are hoping to build on their cup success last time out, while the Steel Squad are keen to bounce back from defeat.

Renato Portaluppi's Gremio have endured a dire league campaign so far, but they are far from doomed in the Brazilian top flight.

The Tricolor dos Pampas held Athletico Mineiro to a 1-1 draw in the second leg of their Copa do Brasil semi-final on November 7, earning a 3-1 aggregate victory and a place in the final against Palmeiras.

In the Brasileirao, Portaluppi's side are currently 18th with 37 points to their name, sitting in the relegation zone with just four games to play.

However, Gremio are only one point shy of 16th-placed Internacional and 15th-placed Vitoria, giving the team genuine hope as the season enters its final stretch.

This week's hosts will also be buoyed by the fact they have lost just one of their last four home matches across all competitions, beating Mineiro 2-0 in the first leg of their cup tie after another 2-0 triumph over Athletico Paranaense in the league.

Meanwhile, Rogerio Ceni's Bahia are pushing for a place in the Copa Libertadores next term, and are currently in position to make the qualifiers, though the pressure is mounting.

The Steel Squad are sixth with 53 points, and with four matches remaining on their calendar, they sit one point short of fifth-placed Athletico Paranaense, and four behind fourth-placed Fluminense, who occupy one of the automatic entry spots.

That being said, Bahia's ambitions took a hit last time out on November 6, when they were downed 3-2 by Cruzeiro, who came from behind to win on a disappointing evening in Belo Horizonte.

As a result, Ceni's men are now within reach of seventh-placed Mineiro, who are a mere two points back in seventh after their goalless draw with Mirassol on Saturday.

To make matters worse, the visitors come into this clash having lost three of their past four away games, drawing once - a 1-1 stalemate with Santos late last month.

On the other hand, Bahia have played one match fewer than Mineiro, and Wednesday night represents a chance for them to strengthen their cushion over their rivals in the race for Libertadores qualification.

Gremio are without midfielders Mathias Villasanti (suspended), Juan Nardoni (thigh) and Danilo (muscle), though Dodi and Filip Krovinovic should be on hand to start in the centre of the park.

Elsewhere, Walter Kannemann is also suspended for accumulating yellow cards, while right-back options Diego Caito and Cristian Pavon are sidelined due to respective muscle injuries.

In their absence, Gustavo Martins, Wallace and Fabian Balbuena look set to start in a three-man defence, flanked by wing-backs Joao Pedro and Marlon.

As for Bahia, they are missing goalkeeper Leo Vieira, who is out for the season with a knee injury, while centre-half Marco Moreno is a doubt with stomach trouble.

If the latter is unavailable, then David Duarte and Kanu should be ready to start in front of shot-stopper Ronaldo.

Weverton; Martins, Wallace, Balbuena; Pedro, Dodi, Krovinovic, Marlon; Enamorado, Vinicius, Amuzu

Ronaldo; Victor, Duarte, Kanu, Juba; Erick, Acevedo, Nestor; Oliveira, Veliz, Pulga

Gremio may be in the relegation zone, but they arrive in better form than their opponents and will be optimistic about delivering a strong performance.

However, Bahia will be motivated by the race for Libertadores action, and are unlikely to be beaten again after their frustrating defeat last time out.

#1700. A Yeboah back in the Premier League? Leeds legend Tony's nephew Kelvin wanted by several clubs in January transfer window after scoring 18 goals in MLS for Minnesota United this term

Published: 04:00 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 04:36 EST, 11 November 2026

Another goal-packed season for Kelvin Yeboah in Major League Soccer (MLS) is expected to spark interest among Premier League and Championship clubs in January.

Yeboah has ended the campaign with 18 goals and made five assists for Minnesota United who finished 10th of 15 teams in the Western Conference, just one point outside and one place outside the play-offs.

It means the season is over for the 26-year-old nephew of Leeds legend Tony Yeboah.

Yeboah describes himself as 'more of a modern nine' than his uncle Tony, who was famed for his muscular physique and his ability to strike with ferocious volleys from distance. He is sharp and mobile with a goal instinct.

Premier League and Championship clubs have been monitoring his progress this season.

Everton and Crystal Palace, both in search of firepower and options up front, are among those who have been linked to a move. Free-spending Ipswich are another.

Kelvin Yeboah is wanted by many Premier League goals after a fine goalscoring season in MLS

Yeboah scored 18 goals for Minnesota United - with Everton, Crystal Palace and Ipswich keen

The striker is the 26-year-old nephew of Tony Yeboah, a Leeds United legend of the mid-1990s

There is interest also from Europe. Hoffenheim boss Christian Ilzer signed Yeboah when in charge of Sturm Graz, after the young forward had scored four goals against his Austria Vienna team in a cup tie in the previous season.

Yeboah has been in Minnesota since the summer of 2024. There is another season on his contract and the option of one more after that.

But he remains keen to test himself at the top of the European game and there is a growing feeling that he could be on the move in the next window.

'As a footballer, you want to play on the biggest stages and express who you are as a person,' he told Daily Mail Sport in an interview on the eve of the MLS season. 'I just want to keep scoring goals and give myself the best chance of that happening.'

He grew up in Italy from the age of three to 15 and represented the Azzurri at Under-21 level. He is also eligible for Ghana where he was born.

At 15, he moved to London where he played non-league football for AC London and had trials at several clubs including West Ham before joining WSG Tirol in Austria at the age of 18.

Yeboah scored 20 goals in a year at Sturm Graz before returning to Italy. He was 21 when Genoa signed him for £6million. It should have been the perfect homecoming but the club then owned by 777 Partners plunged into financial chaos.

Relegated from Serie A they were unable to pay wages and Yeboah was loaned to three different clubs in three different countries before finding stability in Minnesota. He has 36 MLS goals in 79 appearances.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic is reportedly eager to sign a Liverpool star. Talks look absolutely certain at this point as AC Milan look to move.

AC Milan are looking to rebuild a bit after slumping post-title win in 2022. They've only won Serie A twice since 2004, in fact, and Zlatan Ibrahimovic played a role in both.

Liverpool's incredible academy productionThat's before we even start to mention the key role Liverpool played in the development of Raheem Sterling, Trent Alexander-Arnold or Jarell Quansah - who have pretty much become key players for England at senior international level. There's also Tyler Morton, Caoimhin Kelleher, Neco Williams and plenty of others who have gone onto have successful career in the Premier League or one of Europe's other top five leagues. And that will likely continue. Inglethorpe continues to play a key role and Liverpool are leading the race when it comes to their strategic player development. Every season, a new talent earns a spot in the club's first-team and has the chance to showcase their ability. Sometimes, it's even more than one player. And in Andoni Iraola, there's a head-coach at Anfield, who is willing to give them a chance.

Jordan Lussey confirms he has returned to LiverpoolNaturally, not everyone is able to make it at Liverpool. Jordan Lussey was once an exciting young midfielder at the club with high hopes. As a teenager, he scored some spectacular long-range goals for the U18s. Being a midfielder and wearing the captain's armband for the young Reds, he was instantly dubbed as the next Steven Gerrard. There was a lot of hype around him and while he never got to make his debut for the first-team he regularly train with Brendan Rodgers' side at the time, rubbing shoulders with the likes of Gerrard and Luis Suarez. Lussey's career has since taken him to non-league, and the 32-year-old took to confirm on Twitter that he's also returned to the Reds. In a new role working as Liverpool's Alumni Officer, Lussey works with academy graduates who have been released by the club to help guide their career. It's a unique but incredibly important role, and one that can have a positive impact on many young footballers going through a difficult time.
